title: ”Sometimes” I Wonder: The Comedy of Consistency
description: Embracing Inconsistency: The Art of Painting Outside the Lines
imageAlt: A neat sequence of small circles becomes a gently wavering line and a free pencil brushstroke; consistency and permission to be imperfect.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
You know, “sometimes” I feel like I overuse that word – sometimes. Like a favorite old t-shirt I can’t part with. Why? Maybe because it’s a cozy starting point when I’m trying to figure out what on earth to write next.

Human beings, bless our hearts, we’re an interesting lot. We claim to be the apex of evolution, yet here we are, as consistent as a cat chasing a laser pointer. We dream of forming habits, those lovely little routines that make our lives tick. But let’s be real: forging a habit is as easy as trying to nail jelly to a wall, especially if you’re the type that thinks life’s too short for routines.

Now, hands up if you’ve ever felt personally victimized by inconsistency! Does being a tad unpredictable make us free spirits or just… free-range chickens without a plan? And here’s a million-dollar question: How on earth can one introduce a new habit without it feeling like an alien invasion?

Brace yourselves for a plot twist: life isn’t going to hand us a “how-to” manual. The word ‘hustle’ isn’t just something flashy influencers toss around; it’s a cocktail of grit, moxie, and, you guessed it, consistency. If consistency is the secret sauce, then commitment is the main ingredient. Without it, well, you’re just left with watery ketchup.

Thinking about your life’s masterplan? Just look at any legendary figure who’s carved out their niche. Their stories might be as varied as a buffet spread, but guess the two seasonings they all have in common? Bingo! Consistency and commitment.

Imagine trying to break a rock. First thought? Bonkers idea. But with patience and repetition – even that stubborn old rock will crumble. Not that I recommend using your hands, unless you fancy a few battle scars. The point? With the right strategy and a dash of craziness, nothing is truly out of reach.

In the grand art gallery of life, we’re all trying to paint our masterpiece. While the styles vary – some abstract messes, others picturesque landscapes – the magic lies in picking up that brush every single day.

So the next time “sometimes” rolls off your tongue, take a cheeky pause. Dive into its comfy depths. Tackle inconsistency with a smirk, arming yourself with good ol’ consistency and commitment. Because in this chaotic, unpredictable journey, sometimes all you need is a good laugh, a bit of sass, and the belief that every hiccup is just another story waiting to be told. Cheers to painting outside the lines!

Thanks for reading and I hope you will join me in my journey of exploring life and technology.

title: Three Steps to Simplify Life and Combat Overthinking
description: Breaking the Overthinking Cycle: Realigning Focus in the Digital Age
imageAlt: One tangled ink thread opens into three simple clear loops, ending in a small musical wave; letting go of digital overthinking.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
In today’s fast-paced digital age, the sheer volume of information we’re exposed to can lead to a whirlwind of thoughts. Overthinking, unfortunately, has become a silent epidemic. If you find yourself caught in this web of excessive pondering, here are three simple yet transformative steps to shift your perspective and rejuvenate your mindset.

𝟏. 𝐏𝐚𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐥𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐝

We live in an era where influencer marketing is omnipresent. While it can be intriguing and even informative at times, it’s crucial to remember that many posts are driven by sponsorships. Marketing teams have mastered the art of playing with our emotions, often making us feel that we need something when, in reality, we don’t. The key is discernment. Learn to differentiate between genuine recommendations and brand promotions. By reducing the influencer noise in your digital space, you’ll find clarity and relief.

𝟐. 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐜𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬, 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐉𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐕𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐥 𝐎𝐧𝐞𝐬

Heart-wrenching stories flood our social media feeds, often with a plea for financial support. While these stories tug at our heartstrings, it’s essential to remember that not all pleas translate to direct help. Rather than getting lost in the sea of online pleas, why not look closer to home? There’s always someone within our community or circles who could benefit from our help. Shifting your focus from distant, possibly misrepresented causes to real-life stories can be truly rewarding. Instead of just reacting to a sob story, you could be the protagonist in someone’s life-changing narrative.

𝟑. 𝐓𝐮𝐧𝐞 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐞’𝐬 𝐌𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐜

Music has been a balm for the soul since time immemorial. Instead of getting engulfed by the cacophony of life’s uncertainties, let’s focus on its melodious aspects. Enjoy the ambient sounds around you, or dive deep into your favorite tracks. The rhythm of life is everywhere – in the chirping of birds, the rustling of leaves, or your favorite song. By immersing ourselves in these harmonies, we create a protective shield against negative vibes.

𝐅𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐓𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐬

To wrap it up, these steps aren’t about eradicating overthinking but about refining it. It’s about channeling that energy into thoughts that truly matter, that enrich our lives. After all, why squander precious mental energy on the inconsequential? Embrace the song of your life, dance to its rhythm, and let it resonate so profoundly that it compels others to join the dance.

Follow me for more content like this and to experience life in different perspective. Please share this article across your network if you feel this is worth it.

title: A Technologist’s Journey: Exploring Boundaries with ChatGPT
description: My Journey with ChatGPT
imageAlt: An engineer's unmarked compass beside a speech-bubble outline that opens into a path of modular code blocks; exploring with conversational AI.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
In the digital arena of possibilities, boundaries are being continuously redefined. Tools like OpenAI’s ChatGPT offer an exciting sandbox to play in, with an immense scope for personal and professional exploration. As someone who shifted gears from being a technologist to becoming a strategist, my tryst with ChatGPT has been nothing short of extraordinary.

My journey in the corporate world began in 2018, after successfully launching two startups. Starting my corporate voyage as a Dynatrace Consultant, I gradually pivoted into program management, all while keeping my foot firmly planted in the realm of technology.

Utilizing ChatGPT, I’ve been able to explore an impressive array of applications. Whether it was crafting professional emails, curating thoughtful tweets, or even lightening the mood with a dash of humor, ChatGPT served as a versatile tool in my repertoire.

One of the most remarkable applications was scripting a podcast episode. The task was deeply personal, unraveling my raw, unfiltered experiences in the corporate world. Crafting a narrative with ChatGPT’s assistance transformed the episode into a compelling tale that was subtly emotional and strikingly genuine.

The interactions I’ve had with ChatGPT reflect not just my professional needs, but also my personal ethos. I strive to stay authentic in a world that often prioritizes illusion over reality. This resolve is mirrored in the genuine voice of my tweets and the sincerity of my conversations with this AI.

My engagement with ChatGPT also spanned a diverse range of technical topics. I explored JVM Garbage Collection intricacies, delved into the benefits of implementing a web layer before APIGEE, and even coded flowcharts. My use of ChatGPT exemplifies the boundless potential of AI, blending creativity with technical understanding.

My journey with ChatGPT underlines the transformative potential of AI when harnessed innovatively. The corporate world can be a labyrinth of complexity and the guiding light of AI, particularly tools like ChatGPT, can prove invaluable.

If there’s one thing my journey underscores, it’s the importance of remaining authentic and ethical, even when the corporate world nudges you towards compromise. It serves as a reminder that our voices, when amplified with the right tools, can echo with truth and make a real impact.

In essence, my exploration with ChatGPT has been a revelation of the potential that lies at the intersection of technology, creativity, and strategy. It’s a testament to how we can ride the wave of AI, embracing its transformative power to realize our personal and professional aspirations. My journey is just one among many, yet it stands as a beacon for the remarkable opportunities that AI has in store for all of us.

title: AIOps and DevOps — What’s the big deal about them?
description: The next big discussion in Observability and AI world
imageAlt: Two interlocking infinity loops, one around small gears and one around a constellation of data dots; DevOps meets AIOps.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
Everyone has heard of AIOps and DevOps. These are the catchphrases of the 2010s; while the AIOps trend can be traced back to the DevOps culture, the two are inherently different. To the company as a whole, DevOps is a way of life, while AIOps is a step or two ahead in terms of the tools it employs and the technology it makes use of, such as machine learning and artificial intelligence. A good example of this is substituting data-driven decision making for human intervention.

The concepts of “DevOps” and “AI Operations” will be defined in this article. As we go along, here’s a snippet of their backstory. Okay, so let’s get going.

Let’s Start with DevOps

In 2008, Belgian IT consultant Patrick Debois first used the term “DevOps.” That same year, in Ghent, Belgium, he organised the first “DevOpsDays” conference to bring together developers and operations professionals to discuss ways to enhance collaboration between the two teams.

DevOps was created to break down the barriers between the traditionally separate and uncoordinated groups responsible for programme development and server administration. While operations teams were responsible for ensuring that the system remained stable and available, developers concentrated on creating and releasing new features.

By bringing together these two teams and encouraging collaboration and communication, DevOps aimed to increase the velocity and reliability of software delivery. This was accomplished by including testing and monitoring in every phase of the software development lifecycle, as well as implementing continuous integration and delivery and treating infrastructure as code.

In the years that followed, the DevOps movement gained traction and was adopted by businesses of all sizes and in a wide range of sectors. Adoption of DevOps practises has become a key driver of digital transformation across many industries, and the principles and practises of DevOps are now widely accepted and implemented.

The term “DevSecOps” describes how DevOps has expanded to incorporate security, as well as many other areas, such as ChatOps, Artificial Intelligence Operations, etc.

Consider these intriguing DevOps-related ideas:

  • With Continuous Integration (CI), changes to the code are merged into a central repository on a regular, daily, or even minute-by-minute basis. The speed and quality of software delivery can be increased by allowing teams to quickly identify and address potential conflicts.
  • The term “continuous delivery” (CD) refers to the routine of mechanically generating, testing, and releasing new versions of software to users. Teams can now release improvements and bug fixes to customers more quickly and with less risk.
  • Instead of configuring hardware and software by hand, infrastructure is managed automatically through a process known as “Infrastructure as Code” (IaC). Teams can now take advantage of automation in infrastructure provisioning, configuration, and management to boost reliability and cut down on human error.
  • The term “microservices” refers to an architectural pattern in which a large application is divided up into several smaller ones. Because of this, teams can develop, deploy, and scale services independently, which increases scalability and adaptability.
  • DevSecOps is a methodology that merges security checks with the rest of the software creation and distribution procedure. By incorporating security experts from the get-go, projects can continuously monitor for potential security threats and address them as they emerge.
  • ChatOps refers to a methodology where teams use instant messaging applications like Slack for communication and the automation of routine tasks. In this way, teams can consolidate their efforts in one location, where they can more easily share data and automate routine tasks.

Some interesting stats for you:

  1. In a recent survey, Forrester found that 78% of companies use DevOps in some capacity, and the market for DevOps tools is projected to hit $10 billion by 2027.
  2. The same Forrester survey also found that when it comes to DevOps, people value culture and processes over technology.
  3. A Puppet study found that companies who have fully adopted DevOps practises can speed up their code deployments by a factor of 30 compared to those who haven’t.
  4. Full adopters of DevOps practises can bounce back from setbacks up to 2.5 times faster than their peers, according to research conducted by CA Technologies.
  5. Accenture found that when compared to traditional teams, DevOps teams were more likely to have high levels of trust and minimal conflict.
  6. Forrester found that businesses that have implemented DevSecOps practises have significantly fewer security vulnerabilities and breaches.

Now it is about AIOps

As businesses began investigating the potential of cutting-edge tools like machine learning and data analytics to streamline and enhance their IT operations, the term “AIOps” (Artificial Intelligence for IT Operations) emerged in the early 2010s.

Automating incident management and event correlation was an early goal of AIOps, with the hope that doing so would cut down on the time and energy needed to find and fix problems. To do this, we analysed massive amounts of information gathered from various places, like log files and performance metrics, in search of anomalies and patterns that could indicate a problem.

When AIOps was more developed, it began to pay more attention to things like performance monitoring, root cause analysis, and predictive maintenance. As a result, businesses were able to optimise the efficiency of their IT systems through early detection and resolution of problems.

AIOps continued to develop and mature over the subsequent years, with an increasing number of businesses embracing its technologies and procedures. As the IT industry continues to expand, the need for AIOps to efficiently manage and optimise IT operations has grown in tandem with the volume of data generated by IT systems.

Since AIOps can aid DevOps by supplying insights and automating the development procedure, and since AIOps can aid Security by doing the same for the security procedure, AIOps has begun to integrate with other fields like DevOps and Security.

As it allows businesses to better manage their IT in terms of efficiency, effectiveness, and proactivity, AIOps is now widely regarded as a key enabler of digital transformation.

Why AIOps?

There are a number of reasons why a company might decide to use AIOps:

  1. Automation: AIOps can automate many of the tasks that used to be done by hand in IT operations, like managing incidents and figuring out what events are related to each other. This can help organisations cut down on the time and work needed to find and fix problems and lessen the effects of outages.
  2. AIOps can give organisations real-time insights and automated responses to problems, so they can be more proactive in how they manage their IT systems. This can help companies find problems before they become serious and improve the way their systems work.
    Scalability: As the amount of data created by IT systems continues to grow, AIOps can help organisations manage and optimise their IT operations at scale.
  3. Cost savings: AIOps can help organisations save money on IT operations costs by automating tasks and reducing the need for manual work.
    Improved security: AIOps can help organisations improve their security by automating tasks like finding potential threats and how to deal with them and finding vulnerabilities and how to fix them.
  4. Better collaboration: AIOps can help organisations improve how development and operations teams work together by giving insights and automating the whole IT process.

Overall, AIOps can help organisations manage their IT operations in a more efficient, effective, and proactive way. It also gives them the insights and automation they need to support their digital transformation efforts.

Some Stats for Nerds:

  1. Gartner predicted that by 2020, 30% of IT operations would use AI to detect and fix IT problems, up from fewer than 5% in 2016.
  2. MarketsandMarkets predicts that the global AIOps market will expand from $2.5 billion in 2020 to $11.8 billion in 2025, at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 36.8 percent.
  3. Over 70% of IT departments planned to implement AIOps by 2022, per a poll by Forrester.
  4. ResearchAndMarkets predicts that the AIOps market in Asia Pacific will expand at the fastest rate of growth during the forecast period as a result of rising demand in countries like China and India.
  5. IDC discovered that businesses that have implemented AIOps have seen an average 40% boost in IT operations productivity and a 30% reduction in incident response time (I myself witnessewd this in one of our customers in India).

Statistics like these show how rapidly AIOps is being used by businesses of all sizes and in a wide variety of sectors to enhance IT operations and fuel digital transformation efforts.

Final Thoughts

In today’s multi-cloud, hybrid environment, both DevOps and AIOps are expanding. There has been a paradigm shift to using enterprise clouds, which have experienced unprecedented growth and are now significant contributors to the global economy. Because we are the ones who have created AI, we must be better than it, right? If so, then we need to make a paradigm shift in our lives where we can compete with AI and become friends with them. In order for everyone on Earth to live in peace with tremendous advances and investigation in the sphere of technology, we need just dig in and discover the best version of ourselves. Given that not everything we create will have its own unique quality, we must accept that not everything we make will have its own unique quality. To put it simply, that is mankind.

Keep reading and thanks for making this far. I wish you all the best. You can connect with me on LinkedIn and Twitter.

title: Top 5 JavaScript Frameworks and Why We Need Them
description: 5th one intrigued me!!!
imageAlt: Five distinct geometric building blocks forming one elegant software bridge, with fine circuit-like ink connections; JavaScript frameworks.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
All of us are aware of the importance of speedy app development in the modern world. Because of this, I decided to compile a list of useful JavaScript frameworks to assist you in making this happen. We need more people working on improving the world and solving the mysteries of the cosmos, regardless of how far we get with artificial intelligence and machine learning. We can always get better, as long as AI keeps becoming better. As a group, we may improve our knowledge and abilities, and as individuals, we’ll have more time for loved ones. For this article, I have compiled a list of the top 10 JavaScript frameworks for creating SPAs and other online apps.

1. React

To construct user interfaces, developers can use the React JavaScript library. Facebook created it, and they, along with a group of independent programmers and business owners, are responsible for keeping it updated and secure.

With React, programmers can construct modular UI elements that may be combined in a variety of ways to form sophisticated user experiences. In comparison to more conventional methods of directly manipulating the DOM, this one is more efficient because it uses a virtual DOM (Document Object Model) that optimises modifications to the real DOM.

Components, another key idea in React, are independent modules that handle their own state and UI rendering. These pieces are versatile enough to be employed in a variety of different applications and even across different projects.

Given the size and vitality of the React community, there are a wealth of resources at your disposal, including tutorials, documentation, and a wide variety of third-party libraries and tools.

With the React Native toolkit, developers can construct native mobile apps from the same codebase as their online project, making React a popular choice for designing mobile apps.

Many popular services, including Airbnb, Uber, Asana, and many more, use React because of its popularity among web developers. As an example of a basic React component, we may have a look at this code, which generates a header containing the text Hello, World!

import React from 'react';

class HelloWorld extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return <h1>Hello, World!</h1>;
  }
}

export default HelloWorld;

The HelloWorld component is a custom class that extends React.Component in our example. All React components must call the render method, which returns the JSX to be rendered to the DOM. Using React’s render method, you can add this component to your project and display its contents in the DOM.

import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom';
import HelloWorld from './HelloWorld';

ReactDOM.render(<HelloWorld />, document.getElementById('root'));

If you did this, the HelloWorld /> component would be inserted into your HTML file as the root element, which is identified by the id root.

The biggest benefit of using React is that it allows you to easily create modular user interface components. This allows developers to create complex user interfaces by composing small, self-contained pieces of code. This facilitates code maintenance and makes the codebase more accessible for reasoning.

React’s virtual DOM provides an additional benefit. The virtual Document Object Model (DOM) is a simplified version of the real DOM that speeds up the process of UI refactoring. First, React updates the virtual DOM to reflect the new state, and then it determines which, if any, modifications need to be applied to the physical DOM. As a result, the process is quicker than using direct DOM manipulation.

2. Angular

Angular is an all-inclusive framework for creating web applications in JavaScript. Google created it, and the company and a group of independent programmers continue to support it.

Like React, Angular has a component-based architecture that separates the user interface into modular, reusable pieces. Independent state and view rendering is handled by each component. Angular makes advantage of a two-way data binding architecture, where modifications to either the component’s state or the view result in an immediate refresh of the other.

Angular’s built-in directives and services, including dependency injection, make it simple to structure and manage your application’s code. Furthermore, Angular’s robust routing architecture simplifies client-side navigation.

Because of Angular’s widespread popularity, a wealth of tutorials, official documentation, and third-party libraries and tools are readily available. Many major tech organisations, including Google, IBM, Microsoft, and many more, employ the Angular framework.

One key distinction between React and Angular is that the former is a JavaScript library for UI development while the latter is a comprehensive framework for creating web apps. This means that while both Angular and React give a set of tools for developing the UI, Angular provides a more comprehensive collection of tools for developing the entire application.

In terms of code, Angular employs typescript, a typed variant of javascript, and a unique syntax called Template syntax for defining the component’s template. Angular provides a full and potent toolkit for developing advanced web apps that are both scalable and easy to maintain.

The following is an example of a basic Angular component that displays a header with the text Hello, World!

import { Component } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-hello-world',
  template: '<h1>Hello, World!</h1>'
})

export class HelloWorldComponent { }

In this case, the @Component decorator is applied to a class definition of HelloWorldComponent. Metadata about the component, such as the selector used to match template elements and the template used to define the component’s view, can be provided via the @Component decorator.

This module must be imported and then added to the declarations array of a @NgModule decorator before it can be used in your application.

import { BrowserModule } from '@angular/platform-browser';
import { NgModule } from '@angular/core';

import { AppComponent } from './app.component';
import { HelloWorldComponent } from './hello-world.component';

@NgModule({
  declarations: [AppComponent, HelloWorldComponent],
  imports: [BrowserModule],
  providers: [],
  bootstrap: [AppComponent]
})
export class AppModule { }

This would make the component available to be used in the template of the AppComponent

<app-hello-world></app-hello-world>

3. Vue.js

Vue.js is a modern UI framework written in JavaScript. Evan You made it, and now a group of independent programmers and businesses are responsible for keeping it updated.

Vue.js, like React and Angular, employs a component-based architecture that separates the user interface into modular, reusable pieces. The state and the view of each component are handled independently. Vue.js makes use of a two-way data binding system, which means that any changes to either the component’s state or the view will result in corresponding updates to the other.

With Vue.js, you get a robust set of tools for managing the component’s lifecycle, including the Vue reactivity system, which monitors for changes in the component’s state and subsequently refreshes the view in response.

Because of its robust routing system, Vue.js makes client-side navigation a breeze.

Due to the size and vitality of the Vue.js community, a wealth of resources — including tutorials, documentation, and a plethora of third-party libraries and tools — are at your disposal.

Vue.js offers a more opinionated set of conventions for structuring the application, but it also offers more flexibility in terms of the tools that you can use to build the application, such as a template, JSX, or even JS without a template, which is one of the main differences between Vue.js and React.

Take a look at this demo of a basic Vue.js component that generates a header reading Hello, World!

<template>
  <h1>Hello, World!</h1>
</template>

<script>
export default {
  name: 'HelloWorld',
}
</script>

This component can be used in your app by importing it and adding it to your Vue instance’s components array.

import Vue from 'vue'
import HelloWorld from './HelloWorld.vue'

new Vue({
  el: '#app',
  components: {
    HelloWorld
  },
  template: '<HelloWorld />'
})

To compare Vue.js with other popular frameworks like Angular and React, consider the following:

  • Vue.js is smaller and less complex than Angular, and its learning curve is flatter than that of either Angular or React. This facilitates initial exploration and fundamental comprehension of the structure.
  • Conventions with an opinion: Vue.js provides a more opinionated set of conventions for structuring the application, whereas React and Angular are more flexible. Vue’s conventions make it simple to organise and manage the code, and it gives you more options when it comes to the tools you can use to build the application, such as a template, JSX, or even JS without a template.
  • Unlike React and Angular, which require explicit state updates, Vue.js’s built-in reactivity system makes it simple to monitor changes in the component’s state and automatically update the view.

4. Backbone.js

Developed in JavaScript, Backbone.js is a lightweight framework for creating dynamic, feature-rich, and scalable single-page web applications. Initiated by Jeremy Ashkenas, it is now supported by a group of independent programmers and businesses.

Backbone.js offers a bare-bones set of features, such as a framework for code organisation, a lightweight event-driven architecture, and DOM utility functions. Backbone’s primary focus is on providing a framework within which the code can be organised; unlike Angular and Vue, it does not provide a template system or a virtual DOM.

Models, Views, and Collections are the three main components of Backbone, and they are used to model the app’s data and user interface. Models stand in for the data and its logic, Views for the UI and its logic, and Collections for a group of Models.

Backbone also includes an easy-to-use routing system for managing client-side navigation, which enables you to define URL routes that are bound to particular app actions.

Backbone’s small footprint and easy-to-learn syntax make it a good choice for building a minimum viable product (MVP) or a prototype, but it may be too minimalistic for larger projects.

Compared to other popular frameworks like React or Angular, Backbone.js has a smaller community, but its dedicated user base has produced a number of useful plugins and extensions.

A basic Backbone.js view that generates a “Hello, World!” header is shown below.

var HelloWorldView = Backbone.View.extend({
    render: function() {
        this.$el.html("<h1>Hello, World!</h1>");
        return this;
    }
});

The HelloWorldView is a Backbone view, which is an object with a render() method used to modify the view’s HTML. To modify the HTML, use the view’s DOM element referenced by the $el property.

This view can be used in your app by creating an instance and invoking the render() method.

var helloWorldView = new HelloWorldView();
helloWorldView.render();

this will append the view’s HTML to the DOM.

5. Next.js

Next.js is a framework for creating React apps that are rendered on the server. Zeit created it, and now a group of independent programmers and corporations are responsible for keeping it updated.

Next.js provides a number of tools that make it easier to create React applications that are rendered on the server, such as automatic code splitting, server-side rendering, and a development server that supports hot module replacement.

Next.js’s primary benefit is that it simplifies the development of server-rendered React applications, which can boost both the app’s initial load time and its search engine optimization.

Automatic code splitting, server-side rendering, and a development server that supports hot module replacement are just a few of the powerful routing features provided by Next.js.

With Next.js, you can see the effects of your code changes immediately without having to reload the page thanks to the framework’s integrated development server and hot module replacement.

Next.js uses a straightforward file-system based routing implementation, where the route is specified by file name and the component that handles it is specified by the file’s export.

Due to the size and vitality of the Next.js community, a wealth of materials — including tutorials, documentation, and a plethora of third-party libraries and tools — is at your disposal. To demonstrate how easy it is to create a basic web page using Next.js, here is an example:

import React from 'react'

export default function Home() {
  return <h1>Hello, World!</h1>
}

The Home component is defined as a basic functional component that displays a “Hello, World!” h1 tag.

Upon initialization, this component will be rendered as your application’s root and can be accessed via the ‘/’ route.

Next.js is a powerful framework that provides a set of features to easily create fast, server-rendered React applications; it is widely used to create high-performance web apps; and it is great for building an isomorphic web app, which can run on the client and the server.

Final Thoughts

For creating dynamic websites, many developers favour one of several well-known JavaScript frameworks, such as React, Angular, Vue.js, Backbone.js, or Next.js. Each has advantages and disadvantages, so picking the right one for your project is ultimately up to you.

A large and active community makes React a potent library for creating reusable UI components. It’s widely used for developing mobile apps with the React Native framework, and it’s fantastic for constructing sophisticated user interfaces.

Angular is an extensive, community-supported framework for creating dynamic websites and web apps. It gives you everything you need to create sophisticated web applications that are both scalable and easy to maintain.

Vue.js is a lightweight, simple, and flexible framework for creating advanced user interfaces.

For the development of single-page web applications and the organisation of their code, Backbone.js is an efficient and unobtrusive framework. While it works well for smaller and medium-sized projects, its sparseness may make it unsuitable for more involved endeavours.

Next.js is a robust framework that facilitates the development of quick, server-rendered React apps. It’s great for making isomorphic web apps, or ones that work equally well on both the client and the server, and it’s used extensively for developing high-performance web apps.

Thanks for reading. Feel free to connect with me on LinkedIn or on Twitter. Also, follow for more. Be well.

title: Adrenaline for Happiness
description: Mistakes, People, and Money — Three steps for serenity
imageAlt: A balanced arrangement of three stones beside two open hands releasing a small coin and a paper mistake; mistakes, people and money as lessons for happiness.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
Today I am going to write about a kind of scenario that happened In my life and around me. We all know how money plays an important role in our life, right? Even though these days money has gained importance more than eating food because to eat one should have money. Till yesterday I was in a bad shape with life and I was thinking, “Nothing for me in this world to see as I am so exhausted from looking after my parents and some friends who I had to choose between just to be with them.” The worst part, I even thought about taking sleeping pills and sleeping forever — I was in that mental condition because I had no money — They say empty pockets teach us millions of things but not everybody here is able people to endure the pain of lack of money.

That is how life is. It is ruthless and hard. The reason why I am telling this is to say how life changes in an instant. Somebody like me who was completely broken a day before and now I am writing an article to tell their world that if you are in pain, that’s okay and things will get better in life after some series of small gestures from the people around you.

Find your happiness especially that adrenaline boost that keeps you breathing. Let me break it into 3 parts so that you can understand what I am writing. Mistakes, People, and Money.

Mistakes

We all do mistakes in our lifetime there are infinite times we wonder if we could have done better. I did many mistakes too as I made my parents suffer the loss of me running away from home for 3 years to achieve my dream, I failed to self-sustain and also I did a mistake in taking the right decisions at the right time in life so I ended up landing nowhere in life.

Even after all this, one good thing that happened is that I can accept the mistakes I did and learn from them. Acknowledging that we did something is the first step for you to release yourself from the burden inside you. This alone will not make you happy but at least it will free your mind a bit for the next process. So, I suggest, try to accept your mistakes. How to do that? Self-reflection.

“Know yourself by making your mind to talk less to you and see the actions you did as it is. Neither in other’s perspective nor yours.”

Once you can see yourself as you are then the truth about the current situation you are in will start to come toward you. It is the easiest way for you to release yourself from the prison you have created for yourself. Still, my dad never understood the mistakes that he made in his life and I think he will never do that because he doesn’t know what self-reflection is.

If you are such a person here is a tip for you, start listening to the opinions of others around you and ask them for feedback about you. Don’t ask too many people — Opinions will become biased. This is the first step you can take to be happy in life. Keep those mistakes in mind before committing them again.

People

This is a bit interesting part which I tell to many around me. Remember to have people around you then validation of your lifestyle will become easier for you. Unhappiness is mostly caused by people around you and happiness too. I am not giving any contradictory statement for the sentence, Hell and Heaven are made in your mind. I am just telling people around you affects your lifestyle too. It is not affected only by your mind. So, it is good to have friends, friends who can be there for you and support you.

You might not have bigger goals in mind to achieve or a higher vision — as simple-minded you are — still good friends matter who can raise you from the ground. Along with those good people, give some space for critics too — they are the ones pushes you to be better. Don’t go overboard here, my point is simple, more people you have with you who can support your lifestyle, you will be a rockstar. Why do celebrities or rich guys like to hang out with people like them, not with you and me? That is because the people at the same levels think alike.

Do you know one more thing you can do with people if they are not at your level? You can give your hand to pull them up and make them stand beside you. Even if they go ahead of you so what? Whenever you see them, you can simply say, I made this guy with immense proudness. This will deliver you happiness for a long time. You can set your life to look at people only when you understand yourself — Acknowledging your mistakes — about the current situation.

“Don’t judge people because they are from a different region — Country, Creed, Culture, or Planet — from you. Everyone has their way of happiness and answers to questions. It even doesn’t mean you can talk whatever you can and come to conclusion as they are. Never stereotype anyone because every person you meet is an opportunity to get to know the world better. Even if you get hunted by that individual that’s okay there are still 7.5 billion minds you have to explore and also the whole universe left to take your mind for a tour.”

Money

Third and the most important part of life. It is simple, if you have money, then you will be happy. Until you make money you can’t say money is nothing by listening to some motivational speeches given by millionaires. Successful people always talk to normal people that anyone can achieve what they have achieved but in reality, after reaching the destination your journey always seems to be not so hard because you get that satisfaction when you reach your goal. Money can’t buy happiness but of course, it can make your mind happy and comfortable. Here’s the thing, can you imagine your life with unlimited money, without people around you, and zero conscience?

It will make you mad. Can you imagine life without money, full of good people and high conscience? Both lives are useless. With those lives, you cannot have an impact on this world and give meaning to your existence. Money shouldn’t give a meaning to your existence but with money, better people and the ability to accept your mistakes and correct them will give meaning to your life itself.

As I said, I was depressed yesterday for not having money and having ordinary people around me. I don’t wanted to accept my mistakes too. But today, I have great people around me. I spoke to the most beautiful-minded person I know, Spoke to old friends, went out for a drive, I got a way to earn money and I accepted my mistakes which I hardly acknowledged. So everything turned out to be awesome for me. I suggest you try these 3 steps to attain more happiness in your life.

There is no money without people and there are no good people without conscience.

Until next time. Adios!!!

title: Apps That Works For Me Everyday
description: It always matters that out of 100 how many you use it to make your day better.
imageAlt: A quiet desk tray holding four abstract app-shaped cards, a notebook and a tiny calendar; useful everyday digital tools, with no UI text.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
We in our life use a number of apps on our smartphones. Nevertheless, there are only a few of them that stand out and we often use them the most. In this article, I would like to list the apps that I use most. It might be helpful for you as well to make your smartphone live interesting. So let’s get started.

Note: Apps that I have mentioned here are available in both PlayStore & Apple Store.

1. Notion

As far as my concern it is the best note-taking app I have ever come across. Compared to Evernote & OneNote it is easy to use and very specific to its needs. OneNote is kind of very rich and feature full app which annoys users like me who want to keep things simple.

2. Apple Music

When it comes to Music there is nothing out there like Apple Music. I am using other music apps like Spotify, YT Music, Wynk, and Gaana. Among other apps, Apple music gives the best experience of music with its clarity of music and spatial sound.

3. Twitter

One app is required to share what’s happening around you so that is Twitter. I find this useful to share the thoughts that flow through my mind. It doesn’t really matter how many followers you gain from this, it matters that you put your mind out there.

4. Medium

Reading is very important to a person who wants to learn about life. There are infinite contents out there to read and we will never be able to catch up with them. Based on your interests, Medium helps you to see the articles you might like, and also when you have something to say to this world, you can actually write in it.

5. LinkedIn

If you are a professional/business person who wants to keep up with industry trends, LinkedIn is the best way to see and understand how the market is doing in providing jobs and in technology. Connect with as many as people you can (not the fake ones).

6. Audible

This comes to the last coz, it needs a subscription. There are few audiobooks you can listen to for free as well. Audible is a one-stop-shop for all the books in audio format. This is very handy when you are traveling or on a break and needs some inspiration to fill your mind.

Conclusion:

Here is the list of apps that makes my day better. Do you have your own list? I am curious to know about it as well. There are other apps that I like as well which I have in my hone but I use them when I need them, Goodreads, Spotify, Fitness App, Notes, GitHub, and many others including Google apps like YouTube, YT Music, Google, etc.

Finally, it doesn’t matter how many apps you have on your phone, it matters how those apps are making your day better and productive. These days people use apps to kill time, it is a very dangerous habit to have. Smartphones are supposed to be our assistants but instead, we are becoming addicted to them like drugs.

It is totally okay if that is what you want but as long as your actions are less compulsive, your life will be productive, efficient, and effective.

Keep learning, keep exploring and keep smiling. Until next time, Ciao!

title: Time Management Techniques At Work
description: How can life be easier upon following these tips when your inbox has 1000 unread messages?
imageAlt: A small hourglass beside a stack of envelopes becoming a calm, ordered path; managing time and an overflowing inbox.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
We know how life is. We all know that yeah? It is difficult and also it is beautiful. Challenging situations make it more interesting. In our day-to-day work, we struggle to maintain time even though we all have got 24 hours to spare or to spend. As an enterprise architect, I often get work that is hard to manage. A lot of client meetings, planning sessions, and documenting sessions. I fall into the trap of forgetting highly prioritizing works.

I am not a master in time management but in this article, I would like to cover some of the simple techniques I follow to catch up with the tasks and complete them on time.

#1 Keep your Inbox zero

In our work life, there is one thing we all do in common that is emailing. No matter whether you are at the bottom of the triangle or at the top of it. The higher the level you go, the more emails you get to reply to or to take action. If you miss one single email in between, there will be follow-up messages and also many other things will start piling up.

Your life would be like, I literally have over a thousand emails in my inbox that need to be returned. I’m sure all of my friends and certain family members are like, ‘Oh, look who got nominated for an Emmy and doesn’t want to write me an email back!’ I need a good few hours to just sit and get on the phone.

It is good to reply to important emails you receive within 60mins (Workday scenario). One tip you can follow to be on top of this is, before logging out of the work, keep 30 mins of your time to process the email. Categorize them and sort emails into different folders. I usually segregate them project-wise and team-wise.

I only move emails to another folder only if the action has been taken. Otherwise, I will keep it in my inbox. By doing this most of the days I reply to all the emails I get and move those emails to folders. Result? My inbox will always be zero at the end of the day.

The same process I do when I start my day as well. Mostly my day starts at 7 AM so I take time till 7:30 to sort my emails and make my inbox zero again.

#2 Stick to one productivity tool

“The true price of anything you do is the amount of time you exchange for it.”― Henry David Thoreau

In this ever-changing world of technology, every day someone will start coding their own tools and release them to the market. Choosing the right one is a challenge. A tool should always be having good integrations with other tools you use so that you can see everything in one place. The more tools you use without integrations, the less productive your work life would be.

If you want to choose a tool that works for you more, stick to the basics. One fun fact is, people still use Notepad more than any other fancy note-taking apps. One tool which I use to keep everything I collect from we and also from my mails is, Notion. It is an app to dump anything you want. It is free and also good to use. It is very Intuitive. You can import your existing notes from Evernote and other apps as well.

I am not telling you to use the same tool that I use, but it works for me. So you got to figure out one tool that helps you to dump everyday data from your mind to digital paper or actual paper.

Here is the list of some tools you can use to improve your productivity,

  • Notion — Dump everything
  • Outlook — Emails and Tasks
  • Notepad or Sticky Notes — Temporary note-taking app

#3 Label your priorities

“The root of productivity is in personal priorities. Know what matters to you and why.” — Melissa Steginus

Marking something that is very important to you will make your work easier. When there is an email comes that requires my immediate attention, I use this 2-minute rule, “If you can reply or respond to the mail and time it takes is less than 2-min, I don’t think of putting that email on the waitlist.” I learned this rule in one of my LinkedIn courses.

I label my emails in 4 ways, Work, Side Hustle, Trainings & Invites. These 4 labels make me organize my meetings, emails, and other tasks that I do in Outlook. It works for me pretty well.

#4 Experiment with new tools

‘Nothing has such power to broaden the mind as the ability to investigate systematically and truly all that comes under thy observation in life.’ — Marcus Aurelius

Never settle seems to be a bit confusing statement but it works. Many of us think that experimenting with new tools and adopting them is the opposite of productivity. As far as my concern, as long as I research and be open to learning new tools to make my work better is the opposite of counter-productivity. This helps me to stay open to new possibilities and get ahead of my old traditional self who wants to stick to a notepad and get confused when the content of the pad increases.

Often looking at our old practices in a new way of giving it a break to look for better things out there. Always remember, there is a better tool out there than what you are using right now to help get things done. Never settle, always keep learning and do a lot of experiments.

#5 Keep your tension score always to -1

The truth is that stress doesn’t come from your boss, your kids, your spouse, traffic jams, health challenges, or other circumstances. It comes from your thoughts about these circumstances. — Andrew J. Bernstein

What is a tension score? It is just a number you give in between -1 and 1 which tells you how good your mood is. -1 is always mean calmness and 1 means you are stressed. This is what I give to my mental health at the end of the day. If it is 0 then I am neither stressed nor calm. If I get 1 for continuously 3 days, I will take a day off from work to restore my mental health.

You might ask this question, how can I take a day off, it is required for your productivity. For an instance, If I keep continuing to work even after getting 3 continuous 1s, On the 4th day I accomplish very little and that forces me to push for the 5th day, 6th day, and so on. All my pending works will pile up and will become a big mountain which is very hard for me to climb (I am very bad at trekking). If you love trekking mentally, you can always go ahead with what you are doing right now but if you want to change the fact that getting things done efficiently, take a day off.

What you do in your off workday is very important. Try to relax and read books or read quotes you get inspired the most. No computers or laptops that day. You can use your cell phone minimally and get lots of sleep. This will restore your mental health. When you get back to work after that, your productivity will increase at least to 40%. This is my own experience that I am sharing with you all.

Summary

These are the practices that I follow to make sure I keep up with my work and get things done. When things are too difficult for me, it is always a good idea to take a step back and reflect on what you are doing and come back to what you were doing later.

There are 100s of tips and tricks out there to be productive and out of all those tricks these tricks I found very effective. I am not the one who invented these tips or practices, I am just a follower of them. As I read many books and listen to podcasts, this gives me an idea and those ideas helped me to find my own practices. I wish you find yours as well and I hope these points above mentioned will help you in finding your own productivity mantra.

Keep reading and keep smiling. Don’t forget to follow or subscribe to my articles for more updates.

title: #010921 — Sanely September

imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
In this newsletter, we are going to talk about some of the interesting things about APM industry and also some suggestions on what you can do this month to keep yourself sane.

Dynatrace

It is good to understand what Dynatrace is before getting into it. For now, just know that Dynatrace is currently ranked as world’s no.1 tool for Application performance management. It captured end-to-end data from frontend to backend side and display in its web UI.

Fun fact:

To make sure you land on the right page while typing fast, Dynatrace is also purchased the domain dynatarce.com along with its original domain dynatrace.com.

When we type the name Dynatrace fast, we often end up typing Dynatarce hence our team has made this decision to purchase the other domain too.

DevOps

Trends in DevOps and what will be the future? Here’s what some industry experts say.

#1 DataOps will boom

Senior DevOps Engineer at Rakuten

“DataOps will definitely boom in 2021, and COVID might play a role in it. Due to COVID and WFH situation, consumption of digital content is skyrocket high which demands a new level of automation for self-scaling and self-healing systems to meet the growth and demand.

So far, DevOps are setting up systems for Logging, Monitoring, and Alerting only (ELK/EFK Stacks, Prometheus/Grafana/Alertmanager, and so on) Now, it is high time for DevOps to step up and use available data and metrics to generate valuable insights, learn and apply machine learning models to predict incidents or outages, develop automation which learns itself from the data and forecast capacity to improve budget planning. Many have already started calling MLOps/AIOps to this part.” — Nirav Chotai, Senior DevOps Engineer at Rakuten

#2 GitOps will become a norm

Principal Architect at Macy’s

“A “you build it, you own it” development process requires tools that developers know and understand. GitOps is the name for how DevOps use developer tooling to drive operations.

GitOps is a way to do Continuous Delivery. More specifically, it is an operating model for building Cloud Native applications that unify Deployment, Monitoring, and Management. It works by using Git as a source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications. Automated CI/CD pipelines roll out changes to your infrastructure when commits are pushed and approved in Git. It also makes use of diff tools to compare the actual production state with what’s under source control and alerts you when there is a divergence.

The ultimate goal of GitOps is to speed up development so that your team can make changes and updates safely and securely to complex applications running in Kubernetes.” — Soumen Sarkar, Principal Architect at Macy’s

#3 There will be more migrations to serverless

Site Reliability Engineering Manager at Lifion by ADP

“2021 will be a year to watch for more migrations to serverless .. if containers and orchestration were Generation Z .. live loads on serverless will be Gen z+ .. pay per use will go to pay only when you use model .. pay per use and pay only when you use may appear the same ..but think of running k8s pod-based microservice to running the same on serverless when you need.” — Shivaramakrishnan G, Site Reliability Engineering Manager at Lifion by ADP

Podcasts and Documentaries

This month our suggestion for you to listen is about the life which you can definitely change the way you live.

Amazon.com: The Steal Like an Artist Audio Trilogy: How to Be Creative, Show Your Work, and Keep Going (Audible Audio Edition): Austin Kleon, Austin Kleon, Workman Publishing: Audible Books & Originals

It is an amazing audiobook to start our journey with. Let us know your thoughts after listening to this wonderful audiobook.

Tech Quotes

Here are the top 2 quotes we think is good for you to start this month with.

“Imagination is more important than knowledge. For knowledge is limited, whereas imagination embraces the entire world, stimulating progress, giving birth to evolution.” — Albert Einstein

“Designing program is very important than coding it. If you don’t know how to build a solution and if you think you are the master of programming then a 6-year old can catch up with your skill” — Vikram Shakya (Dynatrace Architect)

Thanks for reading, Hope you like it. For more, please stay tuned to out Talented carrots — One and only newsletter that doesn’t follow rules.

title: Getting Started With The Basics of Dynatrace
description: The AI-based tool that built solution-based for all your monitoring needs.
imageAlt: An open engineer's toolbox with a magnifying lens revealing a simple connected service topology and one clear pulse; learning application monitoring.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
Background

In this article, I am going to talk about the things that you can do with Dynatrace while deploying your applications to monitor them. This will give a brief overview of what Dynatrace can do to your infrastructure and help you in monitoring every layer of the stack you have.

As we all know due to the advent of enterprise cloud back in the 2010s, applications started to getting bigger, efficient, and better. Technically according to Moore’s law, it is doubling every 18 months including the hardware capabilities and the way we write code and use CPU to execute the programs.

As this need increased, demand for advanced monitoring solutions is also increased. second-generation monitoring tools were too manual and it required doing a lot of setups and it impacted MTTR for the Ops team whenever a problem came.

Hence, we at Dynatrace developed a third-generation tool. It was not like we were introduced to the market as fresh comers, we had the experience of AppMon (predecessor of Dynatrace). It was quite a powerful tool but it was not enough to adapt to the enterprise cloud where millions of transactions happen every minute.

It needed more AI approach which should handle problems once they come in with a less human intervention. This was the moment when Dynatrace was born and started rolling out in 2014. To keep it short, we just wanted to give intelligence for your monitoring team where it acts as an assistant by lifting heavy loads. Specifically, our tool is built for those who want to deliver the best software for their end-users.

Technical Terms Used

  • Environment: Dynatrace portal where you can install OneAgent and monitor all the resources. This term is mainly used in Managed installations.
  • Tenant: This is similar to the environment but this term is mainly used in the SaaS deployment model.
  • Cluster: Set of servers where Dynatrace is deployed in. Usually in general scenarios, we recommend a 3 node cluster for high availability.

Getting started with Dynatrace deployment

Deployment of Dynatrace is made very simple by our team. It is like all-in-one software that detects your application processes, services, infrastructure, databases, and real users who use your application across multiple platforms and devices. We call this software as OneAgent — It is responsible for collecting all monitoring data within the monitored environment.

Furthermore, we will discuss how to deploy OneAgent and what exactly it does and how can you make your Dynatrace environment better for monitoring.

Dynatrace has its own USP (Unique selling point) with its uncompromising technology advancements such as OneAgent, Smartscape, and PurePath apart from deterministic AI (Dynatrace Davis).

OneAgent

It is a full-stack observability software that automatically detects, collects, maps all the monitoring data of your application hosts, processes, services, and databases then encrypts the data and sends it to the Dynatrace cluster or ActiveGate.

Once we install OneAgent on our servers it will start its work by sending all monitoring data to the Dynatrace cluster in real-time with strong encryption algorithms in the place where the data can only be decrypted by Dynatrace cluster belongs to the customer.

So to understand briefly how OneAgent collects the monitoring data, let’s consider a scenario where you have an application that is deployed on the server, and this application is service 1000 customers at a time. Now, if you install OneAgent in that host/machine, OneAgent will start its work by first detecting the most important processes that are running on the host. There is an exception for Windows processes. OneAgent will detect these important processes and starts to monitor them but still, these processes are not deeply monitored.

You can check the status of monitoring on the Deployment status page in our portal. To enable deep monitoring like getting code-level insights, you might have to restart those application processes one by one. When these processes are starting up, OneAgent will inject itself in the code and does the byte code instrumentation — This is where OneAgent will get the capability to monitor code-level insights and also capturing services that are living inside these processes. I am not going in-depth about how OneAgent instruments each application module.

Tips on OneAgent instrumentation:
When we restart our application processes, OneAgent will instrument each of them and starts monitoring in real-time. Data sent to the Dynatarce cluster is encrypted and the communication will also happen via strong SSL. It is recommended that to restart the process for successfully instrumenting the processes. It is not the best way for you to try and restart the complete machine/host after installing OneAgent.

This is because, if there is a lightweight process that needs to be instrumented or if OneAgent starts after the application process is started after the restart of the machine, OneAgent will not be able to instrument that process. Hence, it is a best practice to keep the OneAgent service running on one end and restarting other processes/services at the other end to makes instrumentation smoother.

OneAgent will detect DB queries from Application server side itself. Database is detected as a service and direct DB monitoring is not done. However, you can install OneAgent on DB host to get infrastructure monitoring. This will help you in monitoring DB process and its availability.

Host Groups
When we are installing OneAgent on any host, we will set an important parameter that is the host group. Host groups are the sets of hosts that perform similar functions or belongs to the same application/team, for example, a host group can consist of all the servers that an application runs on. If it is a multi-tier application or even it is a single-tier application. Host groups can have one or more hosts in them.

Naming Host groups or creating them is completely left to the user monitoring needs but in Dynatrace, if we create host groups we have some unique perks like setting anomaly detection, declarative process group naming, OneAgent updates, and much more especially for the set of hosts that belong to the particular host groups.

These host groups can be assigned in Dynatrace at 2 times, One while installing OneAgent. Second, using the oneagentctl command after installation — This command is found in the agent/tools directory where OneAgent is installed.

$oneagentctl --set-host-group=myHostGroup

To use the oneagentctl tool, you need to perform the OneAgent service stop and start operation before changing the parameter and after respectively.

You can use the below parameter to set the host group while installing OneAgent using the command line (in both Windows and Linux).

--set-host-group=myHostGroup

Smartscape

Once OneAgent is installed and processes are instrumented, it starts to send the monitoring data to the Dynatrace cluster or cloud. This also involves dependency mapping of all the entities — This means, mapping of server, processes, services that are depending on each other. It is visually represented in Dynatrace WebUI as the Smartscape topology.

PurePath

PurePath is the sole technology developed by Dynatrace even when there was an existence of our 2nd generation tool AppMon. It is automatically included when we install OneAgent on the server. As soon as OneAgent starts the monitoring of services, it will start to capture each request that comes to the server from the client or any interprocess communication. Every request that is captured by OneAgent is called PurePaths. This contains even database calls that are made for these requests along with the metadata which contains the status code of the response, service method, service class, and other code-level details.

PurePaths will also contain sensitive code-level information as well. Hence, it is very much necessary to have the right security in place. Most of the things are already covered by Dynatrace thanks to its strong encryption algorithms. To know more about security, you can refer our official documentation here.

Understanding ActiveGate and Network Zones

ActiveGate and Network Zones concept extends the understanding of communication from OneAgent to Dynatrace server to one more level. Simply you can say, ActiveGate acts as a proxy between OneAgent and Dynatrace server. However, network zones will help these communication happen in the given boundary without creating unintended communications — When there are multiple ActiveGates in place, using network zones we can direct communication of OneAgent to happen to particular ActiveGate(s).

ActiveGate

It is recommended to have ActiveGate installed for better communication between OneAgent and to Dynatrace server. It is measured that there is almost 70% of throughput and 30% network bandwidth will be reduced if we use it in our deployments.

Having ActiveGates in our architecture will help in many ways. Especially when you have large deployment scenarios. If you have more than 100 agents installed in your servers and the communication is happening without ActiveGate, this often consumes the network bandwidth and increases the throughput for the Dynatrace cluster.

Since the communication happens in real-time, the number of connections will be very much higher. If you have an ActiveGate in place, this will help you in bundling, compressing data, routing data it received from OneAgent. Then it will send that data to the Dynatrace server. This compression and bundling of data will help in achieving less overhead.

Installation of ActiveGate
Installing ActiveGate is fairly simple and direct as it supports both Windows and Linux. You can see the list of supported OS here. We can install ActiveGate from the Dynatrace portal.

Tip: You can install ActiveGate along with OneAgent in the same machine. In production scenarios, make sure you have the right hardware to run it.

From the portal, you can go to Dynatrace Hub > ActiveGate > Install ActiveGate > Select the OS > Download the installer

ActiveGate is dedicated to a per-environment basis. It only communicates with the environment that it is downloaded from. Even OneAgent is the same. Before installing ActiveGate let’s understand the concept of network zones. To exactly understand the purpose of network zones, you should know that there is a small drawback in ActiveGate implementation.

Note: Working of network zones and ActiveGate are totally different. Network zone concept is introduced to help the communication of OneAgent and ActiveGate in a specified space of their own.

The drawback of OneAgent & ActiveGate communication
When you have deployed more than one ActiveGate, by default OneAgent doesn’t know to which ActiveGate it should send data. In such scenarios, communication happens in a round-robin fashion. Also, it is the duty of OneAgent to check for the availability of ActiveGate and if it is down, it should start checking other ActiveGates that are available for communication. This check happens every 5 mins. Even if ActiveGate is in a separate Datacenter, it will start communicating with that and this is not controlled.

For instance, if you want OneAgents in datacenter 1 to communicate with an ActiveGate which is in datacenter 1 itself, you need to set firewall rules to control the traffic that is sent. In order to prevent this hassle in your team, we have introduced network zones.

Network Zones are still in early adapter phase at the time of this article is being written.

If you have large deployments like over 100 servers, it is necessary to have ActiveGate. It helps you to monitor your cloud environments as well. Without ActiveGate, you cannot monitor your cloud environments like Azure or GCP.
For AWS monitoring, it is not mandatory. To know about ActiveGates and its purposes, you can visit here.

Network Zones

Don’t worry this is the last concept that we talk about in this article. This is a newly added feature to help OneAgent to communicate easily with ActiveGate without any confusion — 99.9% of times software will not get confused unlike humans but still, when they get confused, we receive outage alerts.

By creating Network Zones, you can easily tell OneAgent to communicate with ActiveGates that are inside the same zone as OneAgent. This will make our life easier and no need to setting up any firewall rules or chasing the network team to route the communication. Simply you can define a network zone and tell OneAgent to communicate in it, and this will start to communicate inside that network zone. As a failover mechanism, you can also define alternate zones for communication.

Creating Network Zone
You can create a network zone in two ways,

  1. At the time of installation
  2. After installation

You need to define the network zone in both ActiveGate and in OneAgent as well. While installing ActiveGate or OneAgent, you can use the parameter while installing using the command line.

--set-network-zone=<network-zone-name>

If you want to add network zones to the existing installation, you can even do that. For OneAgent it is using oneagentctl command and for ActiveGate it is by adding connectivity step in its custom.properties file.

It takes couple of minutes to reflect network zones in OneAgent. You may need to wait for a minute or to to see the communication that is reflecting in the portal.
While changing network zones, please don’t forget to stop the service and then start the service of OneAgent or ActiveGate. To know more, visit Dynatrace documentation

Summary

To finish our first step in learning Dynatrace, here is the summary so that you can refer to it.

  • Background of Dynatrace
  • What is OneAgent and why it is so special?
  • Important components of Dynatrace.
  • Why do we need ActiveGates?
  • On top of that, why network zones?
  • What is so special about network zones and how it is configured?

Happy Reading and stay tuned for more articles related to Dynatrace. In the next one, we will discuss more details on Smartscape and Applications.

title: Internet Communication — How Browsers Sends HTTP Requests?
description: It’s time to see how the browser communicates with the webserver
imageAlt: An envelope travels from a simple browser-window frame to a server block and returns along one sweeping ink route; HTTP requests.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
In my previous article on how technology works, I covered how browsers render webpages on the screen after receiving a response from the server. As a quick recap, you can visit my article at this link to understand how technology works.

This week we will be studying how the browser initiates an HTTP request to get the response from the server. We will go through each step that is shown in this flow.

How browser sends HTTP requests?

High-level communication flow from the browser to the server which goes through certain steps before sending/receiving the data. This is not one-way communication. It is the 2-way street where before reaching the server, the browser tries to connect to the server and vice-versa. If anyone step fails to complete, the browser will not successfully reach the destination server with the IP.

#1 Looking for DNS

Finding DNS is like searching for the love of the HTTP request’s life. It keeps searching all the available cache servers before searching in global DNS servers (Like Matrimony sites). 4 types of cache are available by default, Browser, OS, Router, and ISP. There are other types as well where we can use our own caching servers. Those advanced topics we will see in the future. For now, knowing the type of available caches is important.

#2 DNS Server — How it works?

Once the request goes out of the browser after checking the ISP cache for the IP address for the DNS, it hits multiple DNS servers across the internet to find the right IP address for you (If you can’t find a girl in this country you can always try in others). This uses a recursive method to find the different name servers (NS) associated with the domain name. So the search keeps happening until it finds the right NS. This request nature is small packets that contain details of the source and destination IPs. When it hits the right name server, it gets the DNS address of the DNS and is sent back to the browser.

#3 TCP/IP Connection

It follows a 3-way handshake to get this done, like asking if it is available to take a new connection from the server. If the server responds with yes, then the browser will send the acknowledgment to the server.

#4 Sending HTTP requests

With the type of request specified, the browser will send the information to fetch the required web pages from the server. It uses different headers to send the request. Based on this header authentication, the server will respond to the request and send the HTML formatted web page to the browser.

Summary:

In summary, if we see step by step sending a request to the server/datacenter, it all starts with the user who enters the web address or interacts with the application they are using. Before sending requests to the internet, the browser checks for its internal cache and then checks the OS cache then it checks for router cache. If it fails to find the right IP, it goes on and checks with Internet service providers. Even now if it fails to get the right IP for the mentioned DNS, it starts to check in internet DNS servers that are globally available.

In DNS, each domain has different nameservers where it connects to respective servers that hold these domain names. For example, .com (root level & top-level domain) will go to a different nameserver, and google (2nd level domain) will go to another nameserver. Then now this google.com will go and check for the third-level domain name server in the Google data center. This process is called DNS lookup. Here browser will get the complete IP address of the server where it should communicate or send requests to.

Before sending an HTTP request, the browser does a 3 level handshake with the server which includes, SYN (synchronize) and ACK (acknowledge) requests. This uses TCP/IP protocol.

Once the server sends the response as it is ready to accept new requests, the browser acknowledges it and starts to send HTTP requests (GET/POST) with headers.

Happy reading. I hope you all had a great week. Keep learning and never give up on your dreams.

title: Internet Communication — How Browsers Render Webpages?
description: Diagrammatic representation on web browser doing its job.
imageAlt: Three transparent paper layers of structure, style and light assembling into a single browser-window frame; rendering a webpage.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
This article will spend more time looking at the diagrams than reading text so 6 diagrams explain how internet communication works. In this article mainly we focus on browser rendering HTML pages. Let’s start with the overall flow diagram of how communication happens between the client (Web browser) and the server (Backend).

Once the browser receives the response from the server as shown in the above diagram (10), the browser starts its work in displaying the received HTML code onto its canvas (window).

Rendering Webpages

Rendering and painting web pages on the screen are divided into 4 steps to better understand the process. There are in-depth steps that are involved to render webpages as it is the topic of some other season.

It all starts with the user who enters the URL in the address bar of the browser. You can see the detailed article that talks about the communication flow and it comes under the primary skillset of a performance engineer. There are around 105 steps that take place before the browser displays a webpage to you.

#1 Content-Type

In this step, the browser will mostly understand the content it is getting to render by the type it is sent by the request header. Once it detects the type, the browser engine will start taking control in the next step.

#2 Render Tree Construction

In render tree construction, there are two trees where it constructs the DOM tree and CSSOM. By combining those 2 trees, the final output it will create and is the render tree.

#3 Layout Operation

This happens as soon as the render tree is constructed. A box model is created in this stage based on the screen size and device data it captures from inbuilt device APIs. Upon the creation of the box model, it starts painting the contents on the screen.

#4 Rasterizing/Painting & Composition Operation

In this, we discuss how the browser paints all the contents that are collected and rendered in the previous layout operations. It collects the data and creates layers using GPU (Modern Browsers). Once Layers are created, it will start painting on the screen and this happens by splitting each layer into each type of content like text, images, or rich media. This will happen for each layer that is painted on the browser window. Finally, we see a clean and smooth-looking web page (If it is designed well)

References

  • How Browsers Work: Behind the scenes of modern web browsers
  • Render-tree Construction, Layout, and Paint
  • How the browser renders a web page? — DOM, CSSOM, and Rendering

title: Five Questions That People Are Asking About Career
description: #3. How can you keep learning every day when you put under pressure in your job or the business?
imageAlt: Five open doorways along a rising staircase with a small compass at its foot; questions, pressure, continuous learning and a career.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
Recently I decided to post every day on my LinkedIn page. while doing so, I was asked some questions about my career. This gave me an idea on writing about them so that even others will get benefitted from them. Answers are quite common but sometimes to see common answers we need to search all around the Internet.

“Choose a job you love, and you will never have to work a day in your life.” — Confucius

  1. How can you choose/create a roadmap for a career in IT Industry?
  2. Is it possible to start a business even while you are working?
  3. How can you keep learning every day when you put under pressure in your job or the business?
  4. How can you write the things you learned so that others like you can use the same guide?
  5. Why share information about what you know in the first place?
