Once we think of our world as a family and all of us are one, there is no question of competition or to be on top. The only thing matters are, how we are moving forward in life as a collective individual. How much impact we are making in the life of others around us.

Conclusion

Well, now I have made my point and it is left to us on how we are going to do it. To make this world an even better place, we can think of unlimited possibilities. Pausing our progress is sometimes the best solution as individually we pause for sometime when things are not well. When we are facing a crisis in our personal lives, we do take a step back and assess the situation and then move forward — This principle is true even for all humanity. Currently, we are facing a crisis. Many of us may think that there is nothing wrong: I can say, we are wrong in this. We are failing to look at the bigger picture here as we are all busy making our own life stable. We all need to be prepared for what next to come in 20 years from now.

Lot’s stand together and work together for our future generations. We are here because our previous generation of people worked so hard and left their legacy. We should do the same for the next generations.

Keep Reading, Share your ideas with me and let’s discuss them together, harithsa@thenexteam.com

title: Decluttering From Work and Personal Life to Being A Minimalistic
description: Simple paradigm shifts to make when things get out of control
imageAlt: A crowded desk outline dissolves into one notebook, one pencil and generous clear space; decluttering work and personal life.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
We know how things are these days on the pandemic plane. Unless this situation completely under control, things will not be getting back to normal. So, I am writing this article by thinking myself 5 years ahead in life, and if I am a reader of this at that time, how it should be. Let’s start with that idea as of now. I will tell you why this image is important at the end of this article.

Being at home and working remotely is not only taking away precious time that we spend with our family but also it is cluttering our life with a lot of unproductive stuff. It is not that easy to get on with life like how Jerry rigs everything of the gadgets and show in his YouTube channel.

We cannot just rip everything inside us as most of us don’t like to share personal problems with the world. Human beings are not an open book that says, come and explore me I am open for any experiment you do. We crave for privacy no matter how close we both are, you are not gonna tell me everything you have in your mind, are you? I highly doubt that.

As long as we think ourselves more and more in life, our mind starts to store garbages in our mind like how a computer creates temp files to perform certain tasks. Unfortunately, in computers, if we don’t program the Garbage Collection Algorithm, temp files will just pile up and the resources that are used by the program will not be deallocated. The same thing happens to our minds. By default, in our brain, we have a garbage collector and it clears our memory time and time again — This process we can call it as forgetting. Sometimes, when our thoughts that are connected to our emotions come up to our minds, we will not be able to forget it hence, we need to clear our mind by ourselves like implementing our own garbage collector. We can call this process a custom forgetting.

Always remember this process of how a thought starts and ends. Every single thought will start from not seeing things clearly as it is in life. When you see things from your perspective instead of the things as they are, you start imagining yourself. Imagination turns to Visualization. This Visualization turns into a series of events that lets your brain process this as a Thought. As this continues, this will be added with Emotion. When you reach the stage of emotion, you still have the chance to get rid of the thought but if you fail to do so, it will evolve and become a Memory.

When an Imagination turns into Memory, it is almost impossible to forget unless you replace that with something else, even though it won’t go away from your mind, it will just be buried within. This process is true for everything irrespective of the nature of the imagination. The more positive the imagination is, then it gets only better. If you ever imagine the wrong things as I said above like seeing things only in your perspective, it will only multiply and make that memory stronger and this negative thought will make you weak. This collection of unwanted thoughts in mind and converting these thoughts into a memory, we can call this as Intentional Cluttering.

As J. Krishnamurti asks everyone this question,

Is there a thinking without the word?

Carefully, ask yourself this question, can you ever think of something without the word think? This will help us to move forward to the next section of this article. How to declutter your mind from overthinking?

There are 3 ways you can do to declutter your mind. These points might be the ones that you have known for a long time but you are struggling to keep up or execute them.

  1. Keep everything simple
  2. Assessing yourself every day
  3. Spend at least 30 mins every day to do what you love.

Keep Everything Simple

We think our lives are complicated and this is true in certain cases. I am not imposing that life should be simple but when you overthink something or you give power to your brain to process negative thoughts for a longer period, it will be rooted deeper into your subconscious. Here is a simple trick on what you can do when you feel that you are thinking about something too much.

  • Step aside from the moment and divert yourself to doing something else. Changing tracks for some time to move away from the moving obstacle that is cruising toward you is a better choice than speeding yourself and banging into it.
  • Have a ritual that inspires you and keep repeating it. This will prevent any negative thoughts in your mind to go deeper. Usually, I repeat myself, “World is waiting for me to embrace its greatness” or I chant the prayer (Prayer can be anything as long as it is pure).
  • Look at the things as they are, simplify your world. Talk to the person you love or sometimes even you can go ahead and irritate them as long as you can if you feel they can bear your nonsense. I do it so many times to the person I trust and who is mean special to me. In your life, there may be multiple people but this still works for multiple people as well.

To summarize the first point that I am making here, always keep things simple. If you ever want to make a decision that is conflicting your interest or begging you to choose between that or this, don’t put pressure on yourself. Choose the one that is simpler and won’t make your life complicated. Take time to decide and never make promises when you are happy and don’t make decisions when you are angry.

Assessing Your Emotional Goals Everyday

Finding your way back in anything easy as long as you have an anchor with you to pull you back in. That anchor can be your goal in life or ambition. It is easy to forget why we started or even why we are living our lives with all the distractions that are happening around in this modern world. Revisiting your goals every day will keep you in check with the purpose of life. Some might be having a different approach to this, they just go with the flow and don’t think of the endgame. One way or the other going with the flow is also a goal that you have, right?

We might be careful in life but when we start to think several things at a time, we might get stuck and the phase where we fail to decide or even indulging in the things that matter less to our lives can clutter your mind as well. Like spending more than 2 hours of your day using smartphones or checking social media posts that don’t matter or even judging other people based on the news about them in media can affect your mental health and makes you desperate in life. When you feel this way, this means you definitely need to declutter your mind. How you do it? By revisiting the fact that why you started your journey you had set out. Check your goals or a goal.

  • It is good to write down your endgame of life on a sheet of paper and refer to it regularly.
  • Always have that badass vision for your life. Even if you don’t reach that desired level, that is completely cool.
  • Think yourself always 5 years ahead in life. I am not telling you not to live in present or got with the flow. Keep your goal level to maximum. Be crazy — This will make your mind to tackle problems with an open heart — Open heartedness will help you solve problems faster by letting you manufacture brilliant ideas.

Problems can’t be solved by the same kind of thinking that has created them. — Albert Einstein

Spending At Least 30 Minutes Everyday To Do What You Love

You may walk, run, quarrel, listen, sneak out, or hookup doesn’t matter as long as you love it while you are doing it. Are you quarreling with your friend or a partner? As long as you are doing it with Love, it will not impact on anyone’s life negatively. The reason I am telling you this is that the human brain works in a very simple way but I don’t know why people make it so complicated. As long as we do what we love, our minds will never get cluttered. It is the perfect medicine for decluttering in any place (Work or Personal).

Spend at least 30 minutes in your day to do the thing you love in life. Do you love to write a program? Code. Are you interested in Writing? Sit tight and write something or anything. Do you love to read books? Read it or purchase a new one. One interesting thing is, do you want to irritate the person you love? Do it. Irritate them like anything — Don’t worry they will not go anywhere or leave you for irritating them, instead they love you more and more. You can even try other things as well like, Photography, Social Media, Flirting, Drawing, or Going out and exploring the world.

These 30 minutes can be split time. I prefer to take it one shot as this will give some sense of accomplishment for the day. Some days, I feel good and proud about these 30 minutes than the rest of 23 and half hours of the day. I usually write articles when I feel my life is getting boring of I feel like I am over thinking too much. Writing is one thing among many things that I love but no other thing can give me much satisfaction than writing.

  • Find your specific interest in something doesn’t matter as long as it won’t hurt anyone around you to the feelings. One thing I never love to do is being dishonest or betray so do you.
  • Make that interest to stick with you. We all like to get immediate results for the work we have done so, publish your work what you do. It will give you a sense of completeness. You can also talk to someone and get their appreciation for the work you do on that day. Journaling is the best idea for introverts.
  • Do it every day. There is no exception to it. (There is for some like quarreling. I am just talking about productive things) 30 minutes, consider yourself that you don’t have a choice.

Conclusion

At the start, I told you that the image I have created is required and I will come back to it. The reason I decided to read this like 5-year-old me is to measure the maturity level of my skill and how far I have come in my life. The last 5 years made me experience bad things in life as I dropped out of college and got betrayed by the people I cared about. My business was shut down and also I had to leave my family in pursuit of my start-up for 3 years. I had an accident, lost friends, gained some amazing people in my life, Humiliated, Lost myself. All this happened in the last 5 years but again today am here writing this article and hoping that my words will inspire you to be better and adapt few things that I adapted to declutter my mind using the above methods.

The next 5 years will be different for me. I am sure of it. Decluttering life is not just about gaining freedom from your thoughts, it is also about the steps you take to do it. No matter how experienced you are or famous you are, you all feel the burn out situations where your mind only will be filled up with crap. The above-mentioned steps will definitely help you to get back on track. Fro today and also for the next 5 years.

Always remember to keep it simple, assess your goals, and spend 30 mins in doing what you love everyday.

Happy reading and Keep smiling. Be happy. Feel free to connect with me if you have any comments. You can always get in touch with me, harithsa@thenexteam.com

title: Introduction to GIT Basics — Part Two
description: Continued from part one. Let’s understand the next step of how to collaborate our code and some fun stories in this ten-part learning series
imageAlt: Two elegant branching ink paths with small commit-like dots rejoin into one strong line beside a pencil; collaboration and Git branching.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
Part-One: Introduction to GIT Basics — Part One

Welcome back again, in Part One we discussed a very basic concept about Git and how we can sync local and online repository. In this article let’s go furthermore and I am sure this will be going to be great fun to learn. Let me tell you a story before getting started.

The Story — Part 1

There was a city called Git where people used to travel there to talk to each other and spend time discussing their ideas. That place was owned by powerful people like GitHub, Azure DevOps, GitLab, Heroku, Bitbucket, and other board members. They all had their share in the land. But GitHub guy is the oldest member of the board but creative. His experience and share were immense in the land. He owned almost half of Git. So, what he introduced was, he made his land a wonderland and made it accessible to all people. Where they can set up stores of their own and share it with the public or they can make it private. These stores are called repositories. Public stores are called open source and private stores are called closed source (Proprietary). There are different privileges for each type of stores, those privileges are mentioned below.

  • Open Source or Public: These stores/repositories can have owners and those owners can always have keys to the door, but they never lock doors for the people to come and contribute to their stores. Everyone is welcome including all ages. There is no restriction except one, owners can have the rights to monitor the change in store and accept/reject any changes people submit.
  • Closed Source or Private: Private repositories are those in which only people who are close to the owner or a group of people can only enter the store and make changes. It is closed for public and it is like they are hidden underground and those who have access will know this exists.

For this time, I feel the story is good enough and the rest of the story will continue in the next parts as this is a ten-part series. In this article further, we will discuss the following things,

  1. Cloning/downloading repository
  2. How to edit README.md file and the markup for writing in it.
  3. We will push the changes that we did to the README.md file to the online git repository.
  4. Overview of all git commands learned so far
  5. Conclusion

Cloning/downloading repository

Cloning a repository means, downloading the repository as it is in the online version to your local machine. It is almost like downloading the code. To clone a repository, you can directly visit any repository you want and copy the URL of it, and you need to execute the command in the CLI of your system/machine.

$ git clone <URL of the repository>

Note: git clone and git pull are 2 different commands. The major difference between them is, git clone downloads the code, but git pull gets the code from the online repository only when it is connected to it.

Pulling Source Code from Online Repository:

As soon as we connect to the Online repository, we need to pull the code that is existing in it. So, to pull the latest code in the repository, use the below command,

$ git pull origin master

Note: In this example, we are executing this command as soon as we connect to the online repository that is at the end of part one because we already initialized it with README.md while creating repository and GitHub created a file for us. So, if the file is there in the online repo and not in offline means, it is not in sync so we are updating our local repo with the latest changes and files with the online repo.

How to edit README.md

This time I will take you through to the important basic concept of any Project — Documentation. Every project needs to be documented with every detail to make sure everyone who is involved in the project is on the same page. So, for documenting purpose we use .md file and it is a markup file which contains details about the project and the source code that is hosted in the repository.

Let’s learn about it. Do you remember in our previous article, we synced both online and offline repository? Now it is time for us to go to that folder in your machine.

In that folder, we can see a README.md file that is there. So, you need to open that file. You can open that file using Notepad, VS Code, or any code editor of your choice. Once you open the file you may see just an empty file. That is how it looks at the start. Paste the below lines to that file, I will explain each line mark-ups below.

# git-training h1
## git-training h2
### git-training h3
#### git-training h4
##### git-training h5
###### git-training h6Markup options (Paragraph)
[Link](https://google.com)**Training** *of Git* and _its basic_ __concepts__1. List 1
2. List 2* Unordered List 1
* Unordered List 2

Basic Markup/Markdown Source Formatting:

Note: The format of the file must be .md for formatting to work. Also, you can see the formatted text once you push it to the repository. The formatted text will not be visible in any editors. If we open .md file in any editors, it will look like the above code. Upon uploading to the repository, these texts and special characters will get formatted into a readable view.

1. Headings:

Headings are of 6 types in English and so does in markup language as well. In Markdown source, we use # to define the headings, so if the text is preceded by # and space, interpreter considers the whole line as heading 1 (H1) which is the biggest of the other 5. Likewise, if we use ## and space, it will become heading 2 (H2) and it is a bit smaller compare to heading 1 (H1).

# git-training h1
## git-training h2
### git-training h3
#### git-training h4
##### git-training h5
###### git-training h6

2. Paragraph:

Paragraphs are plain text that we insert in the file. There is so specific character to mark this so we can simply write text whatever we want without using any of the special characters.

Markup options (Paragraph)

3. Links:

Adding links to the file is a little tricky. To display the link in any page, we need an identifier text that helps us to understand that as a link and another is the URL or Web address to where that link points to. Below is the syntax of it,

[Link](Web Address)
[Google](https://google.com)

4. Text Style:

There are 2 basic styles we can add to the text. Bold and Italic.

Bold: To make text bold in the markup text, we can use 2 ways, One, we can enclose any word or sentence with ** and ** (At the start and end both). Two, we can use __ and __ (Double underscore at the start and end).

Italic: To make text italic in the markup text, we can use 2 ways, One, we can enclose any word or sentence with * and * (At the start and end both). Two, we can use _and _ (underscore at the start and end).

**Training** *of Git* and _its basic_ __concepts__

5. Lists:

We have 2 types of lists, Ordered and Unordered lists

Ordered List: To create an ordered list, it is straight forward. We just need to use 1. and space and it will automatically consider this as an ordered list. For the next number, go to the next line and add 2. and space and so on.

1. List 1
2. List 2

Unordered List: To create an ordered list, it is straight forward. We just need to use * and space and it will automatically consider this as an ordered list. For the next number, go to the next line and add * and space and so on.

* Unordered List 1
* Unordered List 2

Pushing Code to Online Repository

To push code to GitHub we need to use 3 GitHub commands. git add, git commit and git push

We edited the readme file and the changes are done in our online repository. So we need to push the change to online. How are we gonna do that? Follow me in here,

  • In our command line, we first need to navigate to the folder where the local repo is connected to online. Execute the command as given below,
$ git add <filename/folder/wildcards>In this case, I will execute,$ git add *This means we are adding all the files in the local repo to push it to online. We can specify file name or folder name instead of * as well so that whatever you mention, it will add that to commit.
  • After adding files to git local, we need to commit the change so for that we use git commit command with the flag -m
$ git commit -m “<Commit Message>”In our case, we use,$ git commit -m “Initial commit”
  • The final step in sending all the changes online is the git push command.
$ git push origin master

Note: git push origin master tells local git to push the changes that are committed to online with the origin which we set up earlier and to the master branch (I will explain about branches topic in my next parts.)

Finally, this is how the README.md file is formatted in the GitHub online repository.

Git Commands We Learnt So Far

  • Git clone (URL): The git clone command is used to copy an existing Git repository from a server to the local machine. This creates a directory called the project name on the local machine, containing all the files in the remote Git repository. This includes source files for the project, as well as a .git sub-directory which contains the entire history and configuration for the project.
$ git clone <URL of the repository>
  • Git init: creates a new Git repository. It can be used to convert an existing, non-versioned project to a Git repository or initialize a new, empty repository.
$ git init
  • Git remote: After the local repository is validated, the next step is to create a remote repository that the local repository will connect to.
git remote add origin <URL of the Repository>
  • Git pull origin master: Pull operation copies the changes from a remote repository instance to a local computer.
$ git pull origin master
  • Git add: command to add new files to the local git repository.
$ git add <filename/folder/wildcards>
  • Git commit: command to commit changes to the local git repository. The changes can be any new files added or any existing files content updated.
$ git commit <flags>
Eg. $ git commit -m “Initial Commit”
  • Git push: Push operation copies changes from a local repository instance to a remote one. This is used to store the changes permanently into the Git repository.
$ git push origin master

Conclusion:

So, till now we learned 7 Git commands and also basics about markup language. If you remember, we use markup language everywhere but it different ways like WhatsApp, Instagram, and other social media platforms.

Let us remember who founded Git. Ever since Git was founded, companies and technology taken a great leap in working together. Without Git or Version control system, our software development never would have been this collaborative and fast. Git was founded by Linus Torvalds and he said about Git in his interview,

“You can do a lot of things with git, and many of the rules of what you *should* do are not so much technical limitations but are about what works well when working together with other people. So git is a very powerful set of tools.”

Please find the links below to download and Install Git in your system.

Installation:

  • GitHub for Windows: https://windows.github.com
  • GitHub for Mac: https://mac.github.com
  • For Linux and Solaris platforms: https://git-scm.com/download/linux (The latest release is available on the official Git website)
  • Git for All Platforms: https://git-scm.com

Thank you so much for reading and understanding the basics of Git. In Part 3 we are going to discuss something special. We learn about how 2 or more people work on the same file at the same time and then can merge their changes successfully to the code. Until then, Goodbye.

Happy reading, keep learning and if you have any doubts please feel free to contact me at harithsa@thenexteam.com or sushmita@thenexteam.com

title: Three Practices to Learn Better in Life
description: Learning Without Being Judgmental Helps to Focus On Things that Matters
imageAlt: Three open books on stepping stones connected to a pencil, a listening curve and a small light; unconventional practices for learning.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
Life has some bits of fundamentals and the rest is filled with the lesson we learn in our daily lives. Arguably, we all fight for happiness in life. Without knowing what we need the most in life, we struggle every single day. There is a definite question that has an infinite solution, “Who do you want to become in life?” If I am the one who answers to that question, I choose a way to stay happy and find love in my life with nature. Exploring unlimited possibilities of cosmos and the wonder that it can bring to humanity. Now, what do you answer for the same question? Think about it and I am sure somewhere you will land on the answer that is hidden in yourself.

In our journey of finding answers we often land on different experiences. Through those experiences, we learn how to deal with those situations. Experiences we have always teach us something that helps you to move forward. In this article, I listed 3 techniques that help you to learn better in life. An extensive way of learning using each of those techniques will be explained in upcoming articles dedicated to each of them.

Here is the list of techniques that helps you to learn well in life. These techniques are not necessary to be sequential. These are independent of their own. You can use them to build your life above it.

1. Be Curious — Never stop being amazed for the things you don’t understand in life.

In Einstein’s “Old Man’s Advice to Youth: ‘Never Lose a Holy Curiosity.’” LIFE Magazine (2 May 1955), he said

“The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existence. One cannot help but be in awe when he contemplates the mysteries of eternity, of life, of the marvelous structure of reality. It is enough if one tries merely to comprehend a little of this mystery each day.”

It is obvious that life is full of mysteries. Even now we have a mystery on how our human body works and how it is created or who created. For example, we need food to survive and while eating food, we chew and make it as paste and we assimilate it. It goes to our stomach through the food pipe and in there HCL (Hydrochloric Acid) will be present and it helps for our digestion. Did you ever wonder, how it works and where HCL is produced from the food we eat and how it produces?

Do you know how the universe is created, how it all started? How do we fall when we jump from a building and we break our bones? Why not rain falls down and not up? What is up there beyond the blue sky and why shiny dots appear in the sky at night and not in the day? Why lions are the king of Jungle? Why boys look at girls and feel attracted most of the time? Why it pains a lot when you lose someone you love?

All these questions invoke curiosity in you, right? you think about these questions and think of answers. Most certainly there is no perfect answer to these questions but I am sure you can find some conclusive evidence from other theories. These theories are founded because of the curiosity our brain had. In the past century, we made a lot of progress in our civilization in the filed of Technology, Science, and Human Rights.

This morning I got to know a fact from the book called FACTFULNESS, which says in the last 200 years, the poverty rate in our world has decreased from 85% (The year 1800) to 9% (The year 2018). This is the significant growth that happened in the growth of humanity as a whole. Nevertheless, 80% of all the riches are consumed by 25% of the people in the world but still we are getting somewhere near to make this world a better place to live for our future generations. These kinds of facts blow up our heads and increase our curiosity to learn more about a topic.

In finding an answer on how to be curious, I was forced to understand people and myself. So I started to observe little things in my life even when I felt dizzy and worthless. One thing, I understand is, if you observe enough to know something genuinely, it will open your mind to the new level of thinking. That thinking will unleash the power to conquer curiosity. This how you find yourself to be curious in life. The only thing it demands is an open mind and a little bit of humor in it.

2. Unlearn and Stitch

In this step let’s see how we can use our skill of laziness to unlearn something that is not important and stitch necessary things in our life. Pick a concept in your mind and imagine you are a student of that subject and you are studying about it. Learning about the subject is a good thing it helps you to build your career over it but these days we are moving ahead in technology and inventing new things that we never heard of before. There was no concept of wireless 100 years ago until Nikola Tesla gave the idea of it. Now in 2020, we are communicating everywhere around the world with wireless technology. In the 1970s nobody had any idea about the Internet but now we use it as a freshwater. It plays a prominent role in our daily lives. In this ever-changing rapid transformational world, we should learn new inventions and how to use it. There is no value for obsolete data or skills.

In the corporate world, most of the recruiters don’t hire you if you are an expert in FORTRAN (Predecessor of C). On the other side if you know Python (Modern High-Level Programming Language) there is a higher probability that you get that job based on the job description. This means you need to cope up with the new change that this world is possessing. The good news is, there is a way for you to do that, we can call that as Unlearn what you don’t need and Stitch your previous experience of past to the skill that you newly learned.

To unlearn any skill, all you need to do is to concentrate on some parts of the old skill and take those parts and then compare it with a new skill that you are learning. It is similar to upgrade your Hard disk in the computer or the processor. If you want a new car, you sell your old car or you gift that car to your children. Learning new things is similar. You can also consider this as buying new clothes when it gets old. Likewise, technology is upgrading. I am giving an example of technology but even culture is also changing in this world. As we evolve, we need to unlearn a few things to adapt to the new change.

It is better to unlearn what you know like how old software versions are unsupported to get updates from the developed company, we need to let go of things but the main kernel or the root will always stay the same. New versions are just built on it. Similarly, you got to learn new skills on top of the old one not by forgetting it completely. This is what we can call as stitching.

So in this step, we discussed learning better by using the skill of unlearning and stitch. I will write an extensive description of each of those techniques in my upcoming writings.

3. Observe and Relate

We see things in life and often we judge them. As we look at that situation, a person or a thing, our mind starts to jump all over like a monkey. We get thoughts all over our mind and it is almost impossible to control our mind in that way as it will already be taken control of us. With the practice of observation, we can achieve the control and you know with the control like that, how much you can learn. Always be an observer of your own life rather than a judge. As Marcus Aurelius said in Meditations

“Nothing has such power to broaden the mind as the ability to investigate systematically and truly all that comes under thy observation in life”

There is no powerful learning that comes apart from observing yourself. Learning is not just what you do outside of yourself. It should start with you. When you observe your mind just the way as it is, it will reflect in what you see outside through your eyes. If you see good in you, only good things will be seen outside of you. Observation is an important part of learning something new in life. While learning, just observe for a moment what is it you are learning. Ask questions later.

Once you made an observation of that skill or the person, it is time for you to go deeper into it. This can be achieved by using a relation technique. This technique is often worked for me whenever I felt difficulty in learning new technologies like recently, launched AWS LightSail or Google’s TensorFlow Quantum. Relation technique is very easy to implement for example, if you want to understand how computer works, you can relate to the concept of how the brain works. They both are almost the same. Computer transfer data from wires/circuits to all attached parts of the system, brain transfers via nerves. For every concept you take, there will be a relation. You need to find the relation and attach it to that learning. Once you do that, learning will become easy.

Observe and relate is the technique of sheer creativity and it required practice to master it. This technique does not only hold good in learning about skills. It helps in life as well. It is like for every problem you face in life it helps you to come out of it. Whenever you encounter a problem in life, observe that problem without thinking anything about it. Don’t judge! — I know it is hard to control the mind but you should train your mind to observe. You need not control your mind, you just got to train it. If you don’t judge the problem, this means your problem is half solved. All you need to do now is, relate that problem to someone or something. I am sure there are thousands of people who face problems in life, take help them and take suggestions from them about what to do. Relate both your problems and you both will get the solutions from each other. Think this to the whole company, if an employee is facing any problem or he/she fall out with the company, that problem is not independent, it has to be the same with other employees as well. Contact them employees and relate the problem with the problems they are facing, discuss with them. You will find the answer. See, how this works if you don’t judge. Problems will end. So the prerequisite of Observe and Relate technique is Don’t Judge!

Conclusion

The above methods or you can call this as technique, are found as the result of my series of experiences. To learn more you need to sometimes, act like you don’t know anything. It is a hard technique to do that but to ease this, we can use an unlearn and stitch technique. When you are talking to a person or attending the meeting or the training but you already know the concept. When that person talks about things that you already knew, just ask yourself that is it right to lash on him or mock his face by telling directly, “I know this.” That is where observation comes into the picture. Your honest about that question would be wrong. So you need to act that you don’t know or you should consider yourself that there is something you can learn from that. This is an unlearning technique in use. Be like that person who is curious to learn, unlearn, and observe skills in life. These 3 techniques will never let you down if they are used for good effects. Let me end this article with the quote by Oscar Wilde,

“Never love anyone who treats you like you’re ordinary.”

Without love, you are ordinary but with love, your life will always be extraordinary even little things will get its fortune. So, love your friends, parents, sons, daughters, or literally everyone in the world because there is no one who knows lesser than you. I have never come across a person who knows any lesser. Everyone has their own knowledge to share with the world. Learn and Love are the 2 things that amaze every human.

Keep Reading and Never stop living your life

title: How to Analyze an Application Performance?
description: 8-point analysis for any performance engineer who wants to doctor the application
imageAlt: A stethoscope and magnifying lens reveal a simple pulse through modular software blocks; diagnosing application performance.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
In this technology world, we work every day seamlessly to build applications, delivering services, implementing solutions, or might be serving customers in their environments. In this fast-paced world where everything known in technology is multiplied twice every 18 months. Thousands of organization needs a solution to monitor their infrastructure, network, applications, and end-users. This is where performance engineers come in. Being an engineer is not about having your engineering degree in some IITs or some colleges. No college is teaching how to measure the performance of an application or software that you build or your customers build.

Quality of your applications, Apdex of every user action that the user performs in an application on the client-side to how your application behaves on the server-side analyzed by these engineers. This unique skill comes only when you have the most important attribute in you — An understanding of the architecture of an application. Let me tell you a simple story about how the application works and what happens in the background while you are interacting with it. Let’s dive in….

Imagine you are having some trouble finding a pet store nearby or your pet is hungry asking for food (Pedigree in my case). You are new to the town and you don’t know where to find a supermarket or a pet store.

You suddenly remember Google Maps or Apple Maps and open it on your smartphone. Start searching for the pet store by typing a keyword/phrase, “Pet store near me.” Your mobile app starts communicating with the network. Underlying in the network layer, there will be communication happens that is called the TCP/IP connection.

It points toward a server that it needs to communicate with and it hits that server — In this case, the server can be a physical computer with an Internet connection of virtually created machines on cloud providers like Azure, GCP, or AWS.

In that server, the software will be installed where it is responsible for giving a response to your request. That is called a web server or application server which serves the request from that client — that is you in this case — and sends a response back to the client with results over the network. The network uses encrypted or non-encrypted connections based on HTTP or HTTPS.

I am not talking about DNS here. It is a whole different story though. For now, let’s stick to the point where we all understand how requests and responses work. Your map application is designed to send the request to the webserver with the following content, Location, Key Word — Pet Store, and with some basic information like your session information that usually every application out there will collect based on your consent. When the request is sent to the webserver over the network, depending on your network connection whether it is metered or unlimited, fast or slow, it sends the data.

Once data is sent through the network, the server looks for the program that is designed to process the search and it looks up to the location you are in then executes the algorithm that is written by developers, and then it processes the results based on the keyword and location.

It connects to the database to find pet shops near you. This execution has got a series of steps and actions to complete and all this happens within a second. How cool is that, isn’t it? This is the beauty of technology especially programming and networking.

Now, you got the result and you find a shop near you. Finally, your dog is not hungry anymore. You have bought the pedigree and fed it with it. It is happy and you are happy. So let’s move on to measure the performance of the application. You got results for your search within a second. Imagine, what if the results came back from the server 15 minutes after you query the keyword in maps??? It is better to search shop all by every self instead of using technology right?

Technology is there to help us and get things done quicker than before. Help people, explore unknown places and to expand everlasting knowledge. Using technology for everything where it is not necessary could be very fatal to you mind. You start to show laziness as new invention makes your life easier.

Now let’s talk about the performance of the application. Overall architecture and how to analyze it. Being an engineer it is important to learn these things as you come to work with unlimited possibilities here.

My mentor calls it an 8-Point analysis. He says, “To become a good performance engineer, you must understand the application and underlying technology. Without knowing, a single point among 8, will make your life difficult. Just remember to analyze each application with its heights and level.”

Without further ado, let’s see what these 8 points are. These 8 points are divided into 2 categories I could say. One, DataCenter level that happens in the background where end-users won’t see that happening. The second is end-users themselves — we can call a client for now.

DataCenter level includes Hosts, Processes, Transactions & Services, Database, Network, and DataCenter itself. The client includes Client Machine (Thick and Thin Clients) and Mobile Devices (Browsers or Apps).

So, these are the 8 factors of 8 point analysis. Furthermore, It's time for us to refer to each one of them in detail.

Dependency Analysis:

Part 1: Application level (Client/End-Users)

1. Thick and Thin Clients: (Point 1 and Point 2)

To understand the performance or to detect the issues that are there in any application, we need to understand the application. You cannot simply use Maps without knowing how to navigate. A good performance engineer puts first thing first in understanding an application and know its functionalities. Without that, it is difficult to help developers with measures to improve the quality/performance of the application. Each interaction a user does with that app must be known to the engineer. If not, he/she should take time in understanding it. If they are in a customer place where they are not having access to the application, they should insist application teams show them how that app works.

Understanding the comparability of the application is also plays an important role. I have collected a few important pieces of information you need about an application you analyze; irrespective of the type of device you should know these,

  1. Support for Operating System
  2. Browser Compatibility
  3. Size of the application
  4. Security Protocol
  5. The device it is running on (Smartphones)
  6. User Journeys (End to end)
  7. Session attribute details (Advanced and Optional)
  8. How the browser works and how it renders HTML(5) elements (Advanced & Optional)
  9. Web requests — Pages of the application. Activities in case of mobile apps (Advanced and Optional)

Mobile Devices and Client Machines are the application level points to concentrate on. This is also called Real User Monitoring (RUM) or User Experience Monitoring (UEM) in our Dynatrace terms.

Part 2: DataCenter Level (Infrastructure and Network)

Infrastructure

When you request some data from the website or an application you are using in our case, pet shops near you. The browser requests it from the server. The data is sent from the server through the network depends on the quality of the server and the number of users like you requesting the response for their other queries. Sometimes if there are several parallel users are using the application, the server might slow down in executing the queries and send the response. This depends on server infrastructures like CPU speed, Memory, and Disk IOPS — these metrics are the basic KPIs in determining the quality of the server.

Hence, the first point of infrastructure is the server itself. We call them Hosts.

3. Hosts (Point 3): Key Performance Metrics of hosts are CPU, Memory, Disk. We will discuss others at some time. So, as a performance engineer, you need to know about these metrics, and what causes slowdown and latency issues on disk, how CPU is used, and How memory consumption is causing the issue. To find the root cause in the server, you should understand what is installed in it as well. Let’s move on to them one by one.

4. Processes (Point 4): A Process is an instance of a program that is running on the computer. For example, you are using Google Chrome Browser and when you are open it and it starts running — This is now called a process. It also has the name that is, chrome.exe.

These processes are responsible for applications to run. So now what happens in the host, an application is deployed in it and that application is running and it is built on some technologies like, Python, .NET, NodeJs, Java, and others. A performance engineer should understand that technology based on how they behave in the server or on the host. For the particular application that you are monitoring, you should understand the processes responsible for the application on the particular host. In our case, maps are the application and it is hosted somewhere on Google or Apple DataCenters. These processes have services in which through services, they satisfy the requests from the client. For eg, maps have mapsprocess and it has got a service where it checks for the keyword and gives you the location details for the pet shop. So to be clear, Applications that are running are called processes and these processes have many different services. Each process can have multiple services as well.

If you want a clearer example of the process at an enterprise-level, you can consider your Web Server IIS or Tomcat or Express or WebSphere. All these are web servers in which when they start running they will become processes and when we host the application in it, it becomes an application process because the application is running in it. Before moving on to the next point, we should know the real difference between the application server and web server,

Application Server: Application servers are used to deliver dynamic content like transactions and responses from DBs or any transactions related to business login. In our case, the application server is used to communicate with the business logic algorithm and get you the results for a pet shop based on your location. But, requests must go through a web server to app servers.

Web Server: Web servers are those who deliver the response to and receive requests from the client. If requests from the client are demanding static content (like HTML, CSS content), it will deliver as a response without the intervention of the app server but if it requires querying DB and execute business logic (Getting your location and querying the nearest pet shop), it sends that request to the app server.

Note: Until I write this article, I didn’t know exactly what app and web server does. Sometimes, writing does help in understanding concepts.

Let’s move on to understanding what services are in our deep journey of understanding 8 Point Analysis.

5. Services (Point 5): A service is a software that performs automated tasks, responds to hardware events, or listens for data requests from other software. In a user’s operating system, these services are often loaded automatically at startup, and run in the background, without user interaction. In short, we can consider services as small routines performed on the host/server to execute a task or monitor the events. When it comes to performance engineering, services play an important role in monitoring the calls that are made by the application process. We can also call these services transactions. Each request called by the end-user is served by a service, for example, delivering you the result of nearby pet shops is carried out by a service with a name. Hence, to analyze any error related to the slow response time for the requests, are seen in transactions and services. Response time is a time where a service responds to a particular request upon receiving them via application processes.

The health of a service is determined by its response time, failure rate, and ability to handle the throughput. Throughput is the rate of several requests that are received in a given time. The failure rate is determined by the failures that occurred to the service request or were not able to serve the request received. If there are 1000/requests per minute and out of 1000, the service failed to the server for any 10 requests, then the failure rate would be 1% for that service every minute.

To summarize services, their health is determined by their response time, throughput, and failure rate. To go deeper into it, these services can call Databases. That is what we are going to discuss next.

6. Database (Point 6): The name says, It is the base for storing data whether it is a media or text or even events. Every request that requires data is stored in a database. Almost every dynamic applications use a Database. In simple terms, a text/FLAT file to MongoDB are all databases. The database is often referred to as DBs. When an application process needs to send data that is stored previously to the web server, it calls a service that is responsible to query the DB and get the response from it. Higher the number of calls, it depends on the resource available for the service and Database quality to deliver results. We need not go deep into that now but we found another entity that affects the performance of the application.

When there is a slowness in the application, slowness in executing DB queries might be one of the issues. So monitoring the health of the Database is a job for a performance engineer and process and service monitoring underlying the host.

Till now we understood the end-user level/application level and Infrastructure level along with what is underlying on the infrastructure like processes and services. Now, let’s move on to Network that connects Application End users and their infrastructure. Without the network connection, whatever we talk about will not work. Network insulates the whole architecture of our 8-Point Analysis. It acts as a bridge for communication no matter wherever you are, it still connects as long as you have your internet/VPN connection handy

Network

7. Network (Point 7): What it takes to measure the performance of the application? Consider that you are in New York and the data center is in Detroit, how do you connect to the server? The network does that job. You can also call this the Internet. It uses TCP/IP protocol to connect with the server. How fast you get the result for your query is also depends on the network you are in. You cannot expect to download a file of 1GB within a second with a speed of 10MBPS. So, application performance can also be monitored through its network. Slower the speed of your internet, the more time it takes to send and receive the data. To improve the efficiency of your applications, developers use many techniques like caching, CDNs, Cookies, and other methods. They optimize their code so that the size of the data always stays less so that it can be transmitted through the network quickly. There are 3 concepts in Network to monitor it,

  • Retransmission Rate: Resending of Packets that are dropped while sending data over a network.
  • Packets Drop: Number of Packets dropped while sending the data to the client or the server over the network.
  • Quality: Performance of the network between all the components that are in the same network or on the client/end-user side.

The final point and the most important part of all is Datacenter itself where all the infrastructure is hosted. It can be a huge 100-acre building or a cloud service provider where they have 100s of acres of infrastructure and maintain behalf of us and provide all required services at a cost.

Datacenter

8. Datacenters (Point 8): This comes in 2 types, Traditional and Cloud-Based Solutions. Traditional solutions are completely managed by a company and everything in it belongs to the particular company. Cloud-Based Solution includes IaaS, SaaS, and PaaS services. We rather refer to this as Cloud-computing. Datacenter connects every infrastructure component with the network. It also provides services like Databases, Serverless Computing, and other resource-based solutions. You might have heard of Virtual Machines (VM) somewhere, every host/server we create in this cloud computing is VM. These are created over the physical Computer using Hypervisor Technology. Different VMs are reserved to use some amount of resource in a physical host and that is accessed by you through the network with the right credentials.

The availability of the application is directly proportional to the quality of Datacenter and the network in it. If a Datacenter is down, your application will be down as well so companies often replicate the infrastructure to get high availability. They also use a redundancy mechanism for the services to keep data safe (Databases and Application Status). Monitoring of Datacenter is the base for all components to a performance engineer. One should maintain the availability factor close to 100% with composite SLAs with the cloud service providers (No one can promise 100% uptime of all the services. Closest would be, 99.99999%)

As we see above, this 8 point analysis and the dependency analysis of all these points help any engineer to measure the performance of the applications. In this article, I did not go deep into each concept that has been [resented here but I wrote this article to give any readers an insight into performance engineering. It answers How applications that we use communicates and what are the responsible factors for their performance. I feel everyone who uses technology should know this.

Surprisingly, this 8-point analysis is not discovered by me and I am not the one who explained this. It was explained by my mentor and my senior, Mohammed Ibrahim. He explained it to me and told me how to observe an application when we fail to find the root cause of any critical problems.

Happy Reading and Keep Smiling. Have a great weekend. Also published in linkedin.com

title: A Journey Of Kindness — Innocence of Adaptation
description: The story of a girl with exceptional emotional strength that inspired me in ways that I never imagined.
imageAlt: Two small hands shelter a resilient sapling beside a winding path; a person's kindness and emotional strength.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
Every day in our daily lives we often remember how our life is and what we are doing in it. For most of us, life is all about proving our importance in the environment that we live in. With the people, we do parties with, with the people who we talk to and with the people who think that we are not capable of. Life is all about proving yourself to others with the privilege of having access to everything — This type of life is very common with people who are living in their dogmas.

On the other hand, we see people who live to see their surroundings happy. They are unaffected by the rules of this life. Education, Status, Fame, and Money comes second to them. All they want is happiness and peace between people and those we get in touch with them. This quality is attained by them after understanding their inner self thoroughly. This requires will power, practice, and great observations toward life and the quality of living in it. I would like to call these people as the innocence of adaptation — It is all about the ability to learn and acknowledge their mistakes. Making every obstacle in their life as the stairs of success — These people are unaffected by negative forces.

This undisturbed and undisputed ability comes when we start understanding ourselves. Where we stand, what we do, how we approach, and how we consider a circumstance. When we start understanding about us concerning the people around us, we start to see the change in pour life. As Napoleon Hill said, “We need to mix our FAITH with EMOTIONS for the miracles to happen in our life.” It all starts with a thought and then it will convert into memories that dwell upon our strengths and weaknesses. In this article, I am going to talk about a person who lives her life with all the happiness and unaffected by negativity around the world. Her world is small but still huge. Her circle is moderate but her visions are exceptional. In my years of experience with people and their doings, She is the first person who amazed me and inspired me not only to look at life in another perspective — Perspective so strong that nothing can influence and deviate from the path of success or glory — her story inspired me to attract all the positivity in the world. For the first time, I got the gist of what law of attraction is and how it helps every one of us to become what we want.

I found out about her with her, in the most unusual way possible but yet it is ordinary. As Dr. Happy (Dr. Tim Sharp) says, “To know about a person, ask them first about themselves.” I asked her story from her. She explained it to me in a way that I could understand. Her smile is the symbol of victory she earned by fighting with life and with herself. Her inner beauty is one of the symbols of miracles. Her sacrifice makes her a mother for motherless. We have some wonderful things to learn from people like her where they are the jewels of happiness.

I hope her story inspires you all more than me to build yourself and move toward your goals. This is The Story of a girl with exceptional emotional strength that inspires you in ways that you could never imagine.

The Beginning:

To what its worth, we sustained every challenge that life throws at us. We store memories, collect stories from the day we born in this world.

Once upon a time on the day a girl was born. She has got beautiful eyes and brows where the smile on that baby’s face brought immense happiness to her parents and they rejoiced that day. As the baby girl grows, she started to see the world full of opportunities and the people in it. Her parents filled her life with great values and by observing her family, she started to see things. Her values and the principles she developed as her school and her friends part of it. In school, she made some good friends and saw that world that how colorful it is. She developed a mind to explore people and their behavior and got curious about it. One fine day, “Mom, What can we do in life to be happy and what is the one thing that gives immense satisfaction in life?” the little girl asked her Mom.

Well, her mother gave it a thought about the innocent mind of her girl, called her, embraced her in open arms then made her sit on young mother’s lap; mother answered, “Baby, the most important thing in this world is to help others to be happy and what makes you happy is if you are the one who is responsible for their happiness — An addition inspiration. When you start helping someone, it means you are helping yourself — This will give you immense satisfaction.” Believe it or not, that answer from her mom affected her so much, raised from her values that small baby girl with the cute smile and enthusiasm thought of helping people. So, she wished to become a lawyer one day so that she will be able to help people by giving them justice for what they deserved.

Days went and she grew up to become a little older. 10-years old. She was good at observing people and she was kind to others who were hard on her. She became a good listener. Everybody was loving to spend time with her. Her parents, friends, acquaintances praised her. With the dream of helping people, she started to read books and understand life by asking questions about it with her parents. Her family helped her to understand, live, grow, and encouraged her dreams. She was very good at drawing and doing sketches in her school days. She was praised by everyone with the creativity she had. She was a well-disciplined baby artist. She had a million dreams for the world she’d gonna make.

Turning Point:

At the age of 14, with all the enthusiasm she had, she was dreaming about her life and how it is going to turn out. For every one of us, life gives many chances to become who we are or who we want to be unless there is a turning point in life. These incidents will make us better than what we think we are. It exploits our true potential. There are no good or bad incidents in life, only incidents, that inspire us to take action — Our action decides who we become.

Unfortunately, a similar incident happened in her life. She met with an accident at that age. A major accident that nobody was imagined would happen. It all happened so fast that she didn’t even notice that she was on the bed at the hospital. Her body was completely paralyzed and could not move a bit. Doctors were treating her but her innocent mind is not getting what is happening to her. In the accident, her brain was seriously injured along with her spinal cord and heart. That cute little was never the same. Her dreams, vision, emotional intelligence, and strength were all gone in a flash like our sun exploded all of sudden and entire humanity is wiped out in a fraction of seconds.

Doctors suggested that she needs to be on the bed for a lifetime and there is no way they can make her walk on her own. She was hospitalized for 2 years. Everything for her parents was shattered into pieces. We cannot imagine the pain her family went through. The pain was unbearable for her and her family it was like a thousand pins are throwing at their heart every second for 2 years. Her mother was the one who effected the most for seeing her baby girl who is so beautiful like this on the bed fighting for her life. No motivation can help her family or her this time unless they are motivated themselves as they dissolve themselves in the pool of pain, which will become their only life force.

“When a person left to face with pain every day, he/she adapts to it after some time and that pain will become his/her motivation to move forward with life. Those who break that deadlock will get the opportunity to acquire eternal happiness.” — #ExperienceOfLife

“Pain is enough, let’s find a way to come out of it” her family decided. With a happy face, they all approached in front of that girl with that smile and blistering hope. The girl on the other hand who she was lying on the bed saw them and started to think, “Every day they were coming and by looking at me their face was pale, restlessness and eyes were filled with tears, Now, they are all standing in front of me with the face with hope and encouragement for her to get better.” She saw that beacon of hope in everyone’s eyes that were glittering with tears on their eyeball. This scene of parents trying to inspire their child to get up and have hope about life is so beautiful if that is added with the music of hope, it becomes a great play of inspiration.

She gradually started to believe in herself about everything is gonna be okay and gained strength to make herself strong. That DESIRE to get up and the FAITH of her parents that their child is going to be normal again loaded her with all the ammunition that she needed to fight with her will. She stood up after 5 years of continuous struggle which inspired by FAITH which was mixed with her emotion and great DESIRE to stand for what she believed in life — To help people find their happiness.

Back to Track

As I discussed with you in the beginning that she wanted to become a lawyer and the main purpose of that is to help people find their happiness by giving them justice. She was 19 and her education was discontinued due to the injury. Now it is time to create her education of justice league. This time her friends joined hands with her family to help her reinvent life. As Napoleon Hill mentioned in his book, “Think and Grow Rich” — there are 5 ways of education and to educate is like understanding our strength, and based on that how we act on it. 5 ways are as follows, Own experience, Master Mind Alliance, Colleges & Universities, Public Libraries, Special Training Courses.

Because of the situation, College and University education were far from reach. So she formed the Master Mind Alliance with her friends, family, and with herself to learn as much as she can and never to stop pursuing her dreams. She started to read books, asserted herself as she will become what she meant to be. I want to put this in her own exact words, “After having many problems, every second I fight with mind, my thoughts and of course with my own body.” She dropped out of formal education and started to become her teacher in exploring her soul. Regardless of life which she wanted to live which she dreamt of in her childhood, life made her push her every limit she has and dragged her to become more. With all of these transformations, one thing that helped her to get everything in one place her mind, her body, her heart, and her soul is; her interest and passion toward art and fashion designing.

She started her own business in fashion designing. She serves clients and helps them to bring out the best in them. By her own experience, she learned fashion designing through her art, she reached hundreds of people and inspired them with her designs. Now she is an entrepreneur better than what she wished for when she was a child.

Inspiration:

“The rare people who do become truly exceptional at something do so not because they believe they are exceptional. On the contrary, they become amazing because they’re obsessed with improvement” — Mark Mason

She is one of those amazing people I saw in my life and got a chance to listen to her story. Higher Intelligence works in mysterious ways. We can never predict what is going to happen to anybody or to even us. We only got a present to do something else in life that impacts our future and how we are going to live in it. In this story, we saw how life is turned for a little girl and how she turned around her destiny all at once with her DESIRE to help others.

Currently, she helps hundreds of people and among them, my name is there too. She listens to them each day, requests them to talk to her before taking hard decisions in life where that destroys their life. She loves to read books. She is bookish and rather calls herself as Baby Bookish — This got a nice ring to it, isn’t it? Today her smile is the hope for those who are struggling in life.

Some people still stuck in their dogmas and deceit their minds by not being themselves happy. Going behind money, chasing straight ‘A’s doesn’t help anyone to discover their true passion in life. Every one of us in life, need to understand the fact of living a happy and peaceful life. We are all humans not aliens to each other. We can develop the Master Mind Alliance to become what we wish to become. Egos apart, people together. She didn’t go behind the money of straight ‘A’s in life to achieve what she wanted to become. Her main goal was to help people — That’s it, nothing more. No matter how hard life threw her away, she always had that guts to come back and say I am made for something bigger. I am not giving up.

Her favorite book is The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari by Robin S Sharma. She read books every day as a routine to acquire knowledge. Doctors told her that she can’t give birth to a baby in her life as her body took a lot of beating in that accident. Do you know what she says about this?

“Doc told me you can’t be a mother, that day I was completely broke down in tears. I realized then, ‘yeah I may not be able to conceive a baby but I can be a mother of many orphans….’ and now I am a mother of many children as my 3 pets, Plants and Business to take care of. I am the creator of my life. What made me are my failures, my pain, and my hopeless thoughts.”

How beautiful she stated those words. This inspired me to understand what a person can do when they reach a certain level of pain and win it over. She says that she is the happiest person. Her chubby cheeks, lovely eyes, beautiful smile every happiness within, very fair. At last, I want to complete this article with the words of her about happiness.

“Lots of pain, lots of struggle, lots of tears and lots of failure made me the happiest. All of these not only made myself happy, but others who around me. When you are invincible, whole world will bow down infront of you to learn from you. Be strong and be who you are.”

Happy Reading, If you have your story to share please share it in the comments below.

title: 13 Steps for a Better Life
description: Steps from the most qualified resources that are available
imageAlt: Thirteen simple stepping stones curve toward a modest sunrise, with one open notebook at the beginning; practical steps for a better life.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
Today I am writing about life that brings all of us a series of happiness. We often see our parents, teachers, colleagues, and friends get trapped in life and struggle to get out of the rat race. When this happened to me, I was confused, struggling to discover my purpose in life. Everything around me in life to call it quits and I am not capable of doing something that helps myself and others to discover their true potential.

To prove this point, someone who was the dearest to me said these words, “You are incapable of doing anything in life and at the time of your death you will be surrounded by scavengers, not with people.” — These words bugged me a lot even today I feel down when I remember this. When I was told, my position was entitled to pain and diseases. My mind tried to cheer me up and eventually I had to cut the wound it formed in my heart to get out of life I was in and the people around me. Its been one year since the day I decided to change my life in ways that nobody could ever imagine. I am selective in trusting people so I don’t have a huge circle of people to share my thoughts with. Now, my circle is growing bigger as I am in the pursuit of creating the best of the best. The best of people are not selected by their current situations, The best in one comes from the heart and the potential he/she has in life to do things differently. I call my team as The Next Team.

To unlock happiness in life or to get out of the rat race in life, I have listed 13 changes we can make in our life to increase our value and develop traits that we never imagined we could have. There are 1000s of steps in life and books are available to instruct us on how to build our lives for the better. I believe that when we start to do things we are supposed to do in a way we love, everything in this world seems to be good and kind to us.

Here are the 13 steps/traits I found useful while reading the book ‘Who Will Cry When You Die?’ by Robin S Sharma,

  1. Develop an Honest Philosophy: Always be honest to yourself no matter what. Every time you feel something is not right, think of doing it right. The first step to being honest to yourself starts with your conscience.
  2. Model a Child/Think like a Child: When was the last time you went out on the streets and bought an ice-cream to eat or you asked someone for a gift? Be like a child wherever it is necessary. Take time out of your daily life, and try to be like a child just for 5 mins a day and see what difference it brings to your life.
  3. Wake up early: Early to bed and early to rise, when you help yourself to start your day earlier than you ever was starting, gives you more time for yourself to learn new things. Try drinking a glass of water before sleep, it will wake you up early automatically. Tune your subconscious mind as you can do this. Just break the shackles.
  4. Spend a day without looking at the time: Don’t monitor everything in life. Sometimes, unmonitored tasks are the ones that give you immense pleasure and zero pressure. When you do this more often, your mind will become free and start giving a solution to the most difficult of problems.
  5. Carry a book with you: These days, we don’t find many people who want to share knowledge unless it is work or profession. So, keep a book with you always and start glancing at the book whenever you get free time. A new word you learn, you start seeing your growth in your life.
  6. Have your physiological role models: There may be a god or the person or the group of imaginary people who you want to share your pain and happiness with. Create a group in your mind, whenever you feel like sharing or you need help with it… in life to move forward, talk to those people consider them as your ideal friends. Share, talk, enjoy with them.
  7. Surround yourself with a positive environment or with people: When we are happy, we find the people who are happy and start being with them. The same applies to us when we are sad. So, create an environment where there are people who can cheer you up when you or sad or you do the same for them. Don’t dwell in the past or hang on to the events that made your life miserable. Find people who find ways to be happy and influence you by keeping you happy.
  8. Listen to Music Daily: I found the best possible tracks in my Spotify and I created a playlist of my top 100. This is how I listen to music every day and I am fond of it. I start my day with some beautiful songs from artists like Westlife, Backstreet Boys, and to end my day I listen to my top playlist. You can visit my Spotify profile here.
  9. Think about how you want your funeral to be: Start your day as if it were your last. Begin from the end and visualize who you want to be and how you want to be remembered in life at the time you live and after your death. This mindset is very powerful and will become a motivation to start your day. It comes from the visualization technique to begin from the end. Take a breath and imagine you in the places you thought you will never be.
  10. Become the CEO of your life: This step is simple but yet the most effective. Take control of your life and life will thank you. As John Dryden says, “We first make our habits, and then our habits make us.” Control your emotions, thoughts, skills, and flow in your heart. You are the sole guide of your soul to take it to its destiny. Manage your life as a business where you have to sometimes make critical decisions to avoid bankruptcy. While in making decisions, you should never leave your mission statement of life along with its vision and culture.
  11. Rewrite your life story: As a man you are in your heart and thought, you will be anywhere you go. Try writing your story in your mind and imagine the best possible version of yourself. Understand life as the way it is and the road you took from the past which will guide you on what to do in the future. Don’t cage yourself by reliving the past. Just write it and move forward to the path you always wanted to go to.
  12. Plant a tree: Did you think what you want to leave for your future generation, what would be the biggest gift you can give? There is a reason why our elders insist us to plant a tree, it is a symbol of our legacy. When we give birth to another life, half of our life’s purpose is fulfilled. The other half lies in how we help that life to grow the person or entity to be good and contribute toward humanity and its growth. So, plant a tree and watch it grow. You will get the shear satisfaction possible.

Conclusion:

The final step to improve our life is quite simple and easy. I don’t say what you need to do once you start adopting the above steps in your life.

13. Live life happily and die happily: Don’t regret your life on your deathbed that you haven’t lived your life as you wanted to be. Commemorate your life and realize how big your life was and be grateful for whom you had and the time you got to spend with them. Never take your life where you regret not having done this. Always be an asset for humanity rather than a thorn in it.

Happy living and be the mark upon to the brightest places of your life. Please let me know if you have anything to say to me. Also published on linkedin.com

title: How I Created The Mission Statement Of My Life
description: How did I shape my mission about life and what it means to me — Principles of Life
imageAlt: An open notebook holds an unmarked compass whose needle becomes a single path toward a distant lighthouse; a personal mission statement.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
We always worry about how we define life and in search of the answers, we fall apart. Very few who have started the journey will find their purpose in life at the end. Most of us left behind to travel further distances to find answers.

There are 2 types of people who are eager to find the purpose of their lives. One, the people who have defined their mission statement for life and second, are the ones who lost their purpose of life — these people are always hoping to find second chances in life.

When I started my journey to hunt the treasure of knowledge, I was the second type of person who had zero mission and even I didn’t know who I was. I started to become the lost cause where I had to leave my very basic trait to pursue my wild thought entrepreneurship. I left everything and everyone behind for 3 years and went in search of answers to make money.

I was hoping that things might turn out well for me someday and I will be the one who rules everything. One thing is certain in life, you are always meant to serve a higher purpose, not a selfish money centered life.

As loosing is the best lesson that life can teach us, the same thing happened to me. When I was sprinting into my views and disrespectful thought on the track of life, my tires got busted and the engine got ceased. I stopped at the assist point to end the race of my life.

After ending my race against my destiny, I realized what life is all about and how important for everyone to stop racing and start taking things slower in life. It is easy to race on the track of life but if we go fast by looking at the nice smooth track, you can never be able to know what is happening around you. You may pass the lap 1000 times but unless you stop and enjoy the moment, you will never be able to live your life to the fullest.

Let me share with you what I have discovered in my life.

Principles of life (4 traits to develop)

All the below traits are discovered sequentially and I also tried shuffling them but randomness didn’t work out for me.

1. Consistency:
