title: The List of Best Articles I Have Read in 2019
description: When I started my reading journey, I listed out a few articles that changed my level of thinking
imageAlt: An open magazine with several distinct coloured bookmarks and a magnifying lens; articles that changed a reader's perspective.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
When I have encountered Medium, I was nothing but a normal person and just wanted to read a few important articles related to my coding experiences to resolve my doubts on How-tos. But, now things have changed ever since I decided to reinvent myself. I was working in an IT job and I love the job as well. The same job still I am working. Life was nothing less than a boring journey with continuous knockdowns and persisting emotional moments which I felt I don’t deserve to be like this in life and this is not the life I’ve always wanted for me.

I started reading and made small changes in my life. Those changes completely took me to the next level I am in now. I learned to balance my emotions, control anger and the main thing is I learned to let go of people who don’t respect me.

Precisely I read almost 300 articles this year and also started a challenge #100DaysOfRead in media to make myself consistent in reading. I preferred Medium to read articles and by reading, started to write as well. Till now this process managed me to write 35 articles.

At the time of reading, I started reading articles written by Bryan Ye and his transformation in life. This inspired me to be on track and as he suggested, I started to write 1000 words per day with a timer. I didn’t concentrate on my grammar or any other things. I simply started to write write and write. He is one of my favorite writers.

As we all approached a year-end and already preparing 2020 resolutions, I want to make a list of the top 15 articles that I have read this year. The most inspirational writer for me is Tim Denning. His article about reinventing ourselves, literally helped me to work my way through to earn the consistency to read and write.

Courtesy of Nick Wignall, I followed his steps to read any article or book to understand its right purpose.

Mark Dods, mathematical articles made me wonder about the beauty of mathematics and the base understanding of it. I fell in love with maths again since my 11th class.

I inspired by the writing method of Ayodeji Awosika and Thomas Oppong. I started to adopt their way of writing in my articles after reading their way of writing. They do research before writing articles and they quote those findings around the world and give those articles a unique taste to understand what they are trying to express.

I liked the style of Darius Foroux in writing. While reading his articles, it makes me be involved in them. Every line generates the curiosity of what the next line consists of.

Ethan Siegel’s articles are one for the year kind. His articles are so interesting about Astrophysics/Cosmos that made me love each one of them. As I am also a physics guy and his works are astounding and inspiring. It made me reopen my physics book again and think about the universe from a whole new perspective.

Indrek Lasn — Programming is always simple when we learn to code consistently and master the art of coding. Happiness is always there when we code with best practices. He is my technical Upstander.

The energy of Scott H. Young inspired me as well. His writings helped me to adapt and develop habits that were unthinkable for me before working on reinventing myself.

Brianna Wiest changed my perceptions about life and how to live in it. Her consistent way of expressing about life and living in it helps anyone who reads her articles.

Finally, I found the Asmita Karanje articles late in December. I have read articles of her and straightness in delivering the trueness of the content is good.

Below are my top 15 pics for the year 2019, I hope it will assist you to make small changes in life.

Top List: (Top 15):

  • “How to Reinvent Yourself” by Tim Denning
  • “How to Be a Prolific Reader” by Nick Wignall
  • “The Technology Addict’s Guide to Reducing Phone Usage” by Bryan Ye
  • “The Ramanujan Summation: 1 + 2 + 3 + ⋯ + ∞ = -1/12?” by Mark Dods
  • “11 Ideas That Will Rewire Your Brain” by Tim Denning
  • “How to Get Started on Medium” by Tim Denning
  • “There Are Two Ways to ‘Find Your Purpose’ — Only One is Right” by Ayodeji Awosika
  • “The Universe Is Fine-Tuned, And Our Existence Is The Proof” by Ethan Siegel
  • “15 Ideas That Help You To Get Unstuck” by Darius Foroux
  • “Psychologists Explain How To Stop Overthinking Everything” by Thomas Oppong
  • “How You Can Improve Your Programming Skills” by Indrek Lasn
  • “9 Habits to Increase Your Energy” by Scott H. Young
  • “Be With Someone Who Does These 5 Things For You” by The Good Men Project
  • “The Most Clever Life-Hack I’ve Ever Learned” by Ayodeji Awosika
  • “Set a Word Count Within a Time Limit” by Bryan Ye

Conclusion:

We all have inspired people in our lives and those inspirations are constant. Meanwhile, in our journey we meet some amazing people who are not carving for publishing themselves, instead, they try to improve the lives of others. There are 100s of exceptional people around the globe. I prefer to get inspired by those who make a difference in one’s life.

The people above I mentioned are the ones who are inspirational to me this year. I hope they will continue many more like me in the coming year. It’s my privilege to be among readers to read their articles.

title: List of Books that Changed My Views in 2019
description: Here is the list of books that I read this year and the best takeaways from them.
imageAlt: A short stack of unlettered books forms steps to an open window with a wide horizon; books that changed perspectives.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
2019 has been a year of change for me and yet the most painful one emotionally. I learned a lot in this journey and I grew from zero to something at least 10% in knowing and learning. I call this year as the start of my reinvention. I started to read and write in the middle of the year that made me spend most of my time exploring and learning new things. Here are the 12 books that I read this year and takeaways from it. These books are instrumental in my growth and understanding of life. I haven’t bought them. I just read them digitally. I would love to buy all these books this year. Even though reading is completed, I like to keep them and start over again. These books are good to understand our world and the place in it. Science is on one side and Humanity and technology on the other side.

As my 2020 resolution, this is a special year as we don’t get a year like this till 4040 hence, let’s enjoy more and I am planning to read at least 30 books in 2020. I will be writing articles regarding each of them sharing my thoughts.

Money & Self-Help Books:

  1. Humanity Works by Alexandra Levit
  2. The Laws of Wealth by Dr. Daniel Crosby
  3. How to Win Friends and Influence People by Dale Carnegie
  4. Rich Dad Poor Dad by Robert Kiyosaki
  5. The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People by Stephan Covey
  6. Freakonomics by Steven J. Lewitt & Stephan Dubner
  7. Essentialism by Greg McKeown
  8. The 80/20 Principle by Robert Koch
  9. The 5 Elements of Effective Thinking by Edward B. Burger & Michael Starbird

Science Books:

  1. A Brief History of Time by Stephan Hawking
  2. Cosmos by Carl Sagan
  3. Brief Answers to the Big Questions by Stephan Hawking

Money & Self-Help Books:

1. Humanity Works by Alexandra Levit

The future is now and humans as well. It is important to know that AI and Automated tools are replacing humans in workplaces and leaving many jobs occupied for us. We as humans developed technology to eliminate hard working and introduced machines to work smarter and faster but it doesn’t mean we need to sit back and relax to cut jobs.

Technology is always developed and invented by humans. We cannot neglect the fact that nothing is far more developed than a human brain. Automated tools are here to service humans not to replace us.

A sneak-peak about how technology is replacing humans in workplaces and we all need to make sure to build ourselves to be effective in the future to earn jobs or to stay in any company that pays us. Humanity needs to be always a step ahead.

2. The Laws of Wealth by Dr. Daniel Crosby

This book is an eye-opener who says we can be rich if we enter the stock market and we can double our money in no time after investing it. It is important to know that we can earn money and lose it is in our hands. Stocks are based on human behavior.

When there is a dip in the stocks we get excited or sad to see and we make decisions in the heat of the moment that makes us pay for our mistakes. It is necessary to stay calm and control emotions while investing in stocks. Instead of investing in glamour stocks, invest in value stocks. Look for startups that have promising growths and do not go for investing in a company that has uneven growth.

To become rich, taking a risk is essential but it is not necessary to take risks par with greediness. Holding on to the moment and take 5 seconds break before investing in that particular company. Read a lot of books and if possible have an advisor for investing in something.

3. How to Win Friends and Influence People by Dale Carnegie

The most important values in our life are people and who are around us. Humans are social beings. We need everybody to back us each other to contribute toward growth. The author is suggested we follow some basic steps that are proved to be effective in one way or the other.

Smiling at a person, Remembering their names and appreciating them for what they’re working on makes us likable. It is also necessary to talk with them about things that are important to them. We mustn’t argue as humans and criticizing others is not who we are. We can understand them and be with them eventually, people understand who we are. Humans are always good. They just lack the knowledge to see what is right or wrong.

4. Rich Dad Poor Dad by Robert Kiyosaki

One of the best sellers and my favorite books. This book is about the comparison between 2 fathers and how they help their children to grow. It is about taking risks to be rich.

Robert, clearly suggested that most of the middle-class people just try to be in a race that they never win. They don’t want to take risks, invest money in stocks, real estate, mutual funds where the risks and ROI are high. They want their children to play safe and get a white-collar job and to stay happy forever. These parents never teach their kids about how to use money and how to invest in assets instead of liabilities.

Compound growth effect makes us rich and knowing where to spend money is an important aspect for anyone. Rick people teach their children about taking risks and spending money. Instead of being in a rat race, rich people make their way to grow their money.

He also suggested that only a professional will never help us to be rich. They just help us to pay our bills. To get rich we need to start a business and get a hold of it while we are in the profession itself. Learning from the profession we are in and investing all that knowledge to build the business will make us rich.

5. The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People by Stephan Covey

While reading this book I found out unique ways to work my ways to build a healthy routine. I learned the quadrants of tasks, types of determinism, generations of learning.

With those the top 7 habits that helped me to raise my voice in my head to be good and think straight. Out of these 7 habits, I loved the point that explains to us, to begin with, the end. To assess our value now, we should have a clear goal about how we need to be called in the end.

All these 7 habits like, Thinking about Win-Win Situation, Seeking first, Being proactive, Changing perceptions, Quadrants of work, Experiencing Synergy and looking after ourselves. Really can change our lives forever.

6. Freakonomics by Steven J. Lewitt & Stephan Dubner

Freakonomics is a kind of book that tells us about how to balance the economy and being handled by the money. The economy is not about money. It is often stated as the condition of a person he becomes. We all know about economics and learning to manage it makes sense. From incentives to the goodwill.

Conventional thinking leads to stick to the static growth which is almost similar to no growth condition. People work for underpaid jobs so that they think they will grow at the tops someday. Parents nurture their children in all possible ways so that they can sustain when they grow up instead of teaching them their experiences. In this world, even the names of a candidate matter in an interview.

The authors stated the perfect relation between humans and their economic growth. This book, let me think of management differently. When we understand the obvious that is happening in the economic world we will become freaks at it that separates us from normal people who always want to stay in their dogma.

7. Essentialism by Greg McKeown

This is one of the best books I have read. Before reading this book, I purchased it because of its name and I was not aware of this book at all. I just bought it to read different things that I haven’t heard of. It paid off its worth and changed my whole thinking level.

It made me realize my obstacle and what is essential in life and what is not. I did eliminate the great obstacle of my life along the way. I was obsessed with finding new things and along with my obsession, I loved a person the most in my life. She was the love of my life. She never loved me though. If a person doesn’t love us back, there will be no reason to love them anymore. This made me think and eliminate this part in my life so that I can prevent 1000s of hurdles that can come in the way of my goal.

Essentialism talks about how we can choose decessions and develop that mentality, what we need to do. Exploring our options and eliminating unimportant things in our life often helps us to gain that essentialist instinct. Choose a vital few from trivial many options that are how we can be productive in life. The 3 basic steps of essentialism are to Explore, Eliminate and Execute.

8. The 80/20 Principle by Robert Koch

This principle is also called a Pareto principle. I must say that this book is the brother of Essentialism. One must read both of the books continuously to improve their level of thinking. I recommend that these 2 books are somehow interconnected together. Eliminating obstacles or selecting the right choice that makes a difference to the rest of other choices that these books suggest.

This book helped me to execute the task that I was trying to eliminate obstacles in my life — Love and Care at this moment. In this book author, discussed different scenarios about how we can adopt this rule in our daily lives from the profession to learning any skills altogether. Practicing this principle helps choose the top 20 percent that affects our result more than the rest of 80 percent. We have to choose what makes us grow and take us toward our goal by focussing on it. The rest of the other choices we can say no for this is where essentialism comes into play. Be an essentialist first and then apply the 80/20 principle to tune your life to the balance.

9. The 5 Elements of Effective Thinking by Edward B. Burger & Michael Starbird

The most recent book I have read and the important one as well. Every day is a new start to discover ourselves. A bit of improvement in our life every day can make a huge difference in a year. When we think about the start and the current position we are in, we should observe the change that we traveled through.

The basic 5 elements in our universe are compared to each of the habits that we need to cultivate. Understanding deeply, Making mistakes and learning from them, Asking questions even after getting answers, The flow of ideas and Changing based on the four elements are the 5 habits we can cultivate to think effectively. At the start, I didn’t agree with the author even he spent years research before writing the book. As I adopted each of those elements in my life, the 5th element occurred to me inevitably. That was the time I found out how beautiful this adoption has been in my life.

Science Books

1. A Brief History of Time by Stephan Hawking

Here comes the favorite part. Astrophysics has been my favorite part but never read any book regarding it. From my childhood itself, I have been thinking about reading this masterpiece from a great thinker. In this book, he uncovered every possibility of Astrophysics and made readers understand about space and the objects in it. Starting from the big bang, until predicting the movements of celestial objects, it has explained in layman terms to make us understand.

Laws of gravitation, the theory of relativity, universal laws are explained with examples that govern all the universe. Forces that are responsible for the origin of the universe and the concept of space-time is explained quite clearly. This is a brief history of time from the big bang to black holes.

2. Cosmos by Carl Sagan

A simple and quite effective book to understand the concept of space. Carl Sagan — A great Astrophysicist written this book to help us understand what is happening in the universe and how we are using technologies to contact alien life. There are several questions answered in the process. Colonizing other planets, Exploring beyond our solar system, Current technology improvements, Telescopes and a little bit of Human history about space exploration is explained.

3. Brief Answers to the Big Questions by Stephan Hawking

The final book was written by Stephan Hawking, In his masterpiece, he took some of the biggest questions to answer with his style. Questions like, Are we alone? Who we are? Where are we come from? What are the odds of human survival? Why containing AI is important? What do we need to do to control Global Warming? Every question that humanity is finding answers for are mentioned and answered in his way beyond everything.

He discussed these topics with simple examples and words so that anyone can understand the probability. My favorite part of this book is when he tells us about the death of black holes and the presence of antimatter. He says, “Even light cannot escape a black hole — but something can.”

Conclusion:

So this is my list of books that I have read this whole year. I was able to read the digital copies of it. I like to have hard copies of all of them. Due to some constraints, I was not able to purchase these book but the experience of reading them at hand is far better than digital prints.

These books are exceptional. I think everyone should read these books. The values we can get from reading these are exceptional. They change the way we think about humanity and life. Starting from learning how to manage money to understanding the cosmos with the knowledge of humanity and technology will give every individual to start a new life from a different perspective.

Join my email list in my journey

title: Thoughts of 5 Elements that are Responsible for Effective Thinking
description: Remember the habits that we need to cultivate to break the barrier between learning and thinking. We can only learn when we think.
imageAlt: Five simple elements—water ripple, warm flame, stone, air swirl and a small geometric star—gather around an open notebook; effective thinking.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
As we all know how effective our life will be when we become essentialists and apply the 80/20 principle. Now, I am about to write about the 5 elements that are responsible for effective thinking. This article is the summary and my thoughts about the book, “The 5 Elements of Effective Thinking” written by Edward B. Burger and Michael Starbird.

We like to become great or we talk about people who have achieved impossible things to imagine from Einstein to Bill Gates or Steve Jobs. All those talents are not just developed or adopted in a single day. It has come from generations and inherited them. It is not only about inheritance, but they all also had that character to adopt the level of thinking that inspired them to achieve big.

There are some chapters that I listed while reading the book that will help you to change the way you think to be better than what you are now. I always tell most of the people around me to keep improving and learning. See yourself for the progress of 1% every day. Until I am the one who implements that in my personal life, I never suggest to anybody to go with it. I am the test case for every experiment of my life. When that works for me, I tell others about the effort to make sure it helps them to change the way in their life.

In this article, you will also find a few highlights, tips and try these points from the book. This will also help you to build the character that needs to be strong and collective.

All of these summaries that I am willing to write are in a series of interconnected thoughts. The first one was about being an essentialist — to eliminate difficulties in life by selecting effective few from trivial many options. The 80/20 rule suggests that the small change in life leads to the bug difference hence look for the top 20% to change the rest of 80%. This book helps to think in the ways where all of these holds in an account.

Chapters:

  • Elements of effective thinking, learning and creating
  • Earth: In everything you do, refine your skills and knowledge about fundamental concepts and simple cases
  • Fire: Mistakes and failure are not signs of weakness; instead they are opportunities for future success
  • Air: The right questions are incredibly powerful tools for understanding and learning
  • Water: Successful and eﬀective learners and innovators harness the power of the ﬂow of ideas
  • The Quintessential Element: Adopt the habit of constructive change

Elements of effective thinking, learning and creating

Already I mentioned that great minds are not just created over one night or with a gift from God. Those minds are created by continuous learning and training the mind to be strong by thinking effectively. We will only learn when we create and take risks out of it.

There are main building blocks of effective thinking, they are, Understand Deeply, Make Mistakes, Ask Questions, Follow the flow and Change These blocks are Instrumental in generating creativity in our minds that leads to think and learn effectively.

Authors also suggest that learning is eternal and it doesn’t end in formal schooling. Education is the life long teacher and we are the students who devoted to learning till our last breath. By adopting these successful habits, we can change to our lives even as a student or as a professional. All these habits are compared to the basic elements of earth, Earth, Fire, Air, Water, The quintessential element respectively.

Earth: In everything you do, refine your skills and knowledge about fundamental concepts and simple cases

While I was reading this part, the Authors strongly suggests understanding the basics when we try to know a concept and learn those fundamentals. “If you can’t explain the concept clearly, it means you know nothing about it.” Drill down and understand the topic you are working on. When things seem difficult to start over and help yourself to remember.

I do space repetition to remember and understand the things I read in my past. I take a day in a month where I only dedicate that day to recall what I read the whole month and review them. In Try this section, there is an activity you can do to understand fundamentals deeply (Point 1).

Understanding deeply is associated with earth element as the symbol of our mind that tells us that we are standing on rock-solid i.e. earth itself.

Mastering the basics:

This is very important to understand deeply about any subject. When we learn to code I observed a few people don’t know the meaning of SQL or Variables but still, they put 5 to 6 years of experience as a developer in their resumé. This doesn’t make sense and they are meant to be ruled that is because they are already ruled by the money and expectations.

Understand simple things deeply this helps you to master the fundamental principles, ideas, and methods. This is where you create a solid foundation.

Fire: Mistakes and failure are not signs of weakness; instead they are opportunities for future success

Failure is the mother of correctness. Until you fail, you don’t learn. Every successful people failed a lot of times. The only difference is, an individual who learns from the failures is the one who will be successful. Everyone needs the taste of success and nobody wants to work for it. When a person fails, he gives up and he just throws himself away from facing similar threats again. This can be due to fear, survival or non-willingness.

I have been in such a situation more than once in my life. As a student, I was brilliant in experimenting with my thoughts and explain it to others. Even if they never made sense. My friends were not listening to me and even my teachers as well. This is where I started to fail. I failed to convince and later after my 12th class, I failed to convince my parents that my goal was to become a scientist — precisely an Astrophysicist. After I joined my college, I failed to convince my lecturers that I want to establish a cloud service on our premises where every student can host their websites of their own. I worked every free time in my college that time for that project but finally, they bailed on me and sued me as a student. I had to drop out of college for that reason.

Later I started my own company with my best friend and I loved her more than anyone in my life. Our company got shut down for being so polite and dreaming about bringing change to the education system. The politics of the education system took me away. Later, I had to leave my best friend — the person I loved the most in my life because of the unconditionality I had on her. I loved her too much and when she found someone to love, I couldn’t bear. I had to leave her for good. I failed in it as well. I grew up in a joint family from both my father and mother’s side. We had almost 60 to 80 family members when we were celebrating festivals. Eventually, because of money, they fall apart. I failed to hold them together.

These are all the failures I have faced in my life. And still, I have hope that one day I will be successful in something that makes me good.

Failing nine times:

Failing nine times is a theory that when you fail for the first time, you need to think that you are going to fail 9 times and the 10th time you will be successful. Do this exercise. Check to Try this section. (Point 2)

Air: The right questions are incredibly powerful tools for understanding and learning

Questions are pretty hard things that aid in expanding our minds. When we work on something and if we get questions back regarding this from different people, we often get demotivated. This is quite common among human beings. We stand apart from the whole when we are curious enough to discover and see the great things. Asking questions and thinking about them matters and it helps to go beyond understanding from different angles.

Going from demotivation to ask yourself the question, “What if…?” Every accomplishment you make helps expand your understanding of the concept you are working on.

How answers can lead questions:

It is important to question something to understand about it deeply. Consider Journalists, who ask questions in every angle about the news that they already know to explore it deeply. A child asks a lot of questions even after getting an answer to the first question he/she ask. They create an infinite loop of questions like Why? What? How? What if..? How long..? And, so on… It becomes a habit to question everything. Questioning is not enough, we need to develop the character to answer them or find answers for.

Teach to learn:

The advantages of questioning help us to learn. This is how we can build the biggest technological marvels in the world right now. Science is all about questioning and teaching to those who ask questions by proving them with answers to the questions they ask. When we write software, the quality analysis team asks questions and creates scenarios in which the software can run to prove its integrity.

Try the exercise that is mentioned in Try this section. (Point 3 and 4)

Teach a person or the group of people and get questions from them to learn about the subject deeply. It is really fun. I do this activity with my Mom every day. I ask her a lot of questions about religion and later I relate her answers to science and later I understand what is happening in the world. This is how I learn and explore the world. I ask questions for everything and later I find answers by analyzing the data that I receive.

Water: Successful and eﬀective learners and innovators harness the power of the ﬂow of ideas

Look at the brighter side of life and see how the greatest people in human history prevail. They all seemed to follow these habits. Giving value to the flow of ideas is important and later after giving the value, we must understand it deeply, asking questions to improve the idea and not doubting yourself when a failure occurs. These three elements which are converted to habits will rise as an Ideas or at least happens to contribute to the flow of ideas you have.

Iterate Ideas:

Repeating ideas again and again and getting to the flow of it makes sense to the growth and exploring impossible. Who would have thought in the 1970s that the Internet will become the dominant force of humans in 2019? The small ideas that bring us together to achieve great things. No matter how small the idea is, if it is nurtured with the right resources, it can change the course of our understanding altogether.

These ideas make our world a better place. Ideas are important to lead the curiosity of humankind.

The Quintessential Element: Adopt the habit of constructive change

Without the above 4 elements in life, this one is not possible. There is a say, “The only thing that is constant in this universe is — Change” It is static and yet constructive. We need to develop this character to change for good. When I followed those 4 elements in my life, it demanded a change from me. I never feared for a failure, always asked questions. Tried to change others who are arguably adamant for changing themselves for good. I failed to change them but still, I am successful in changing vital few from trivial many.

The biggest success I have have ever had till now is myself. I am now, accepting what it is there. My flow of ideas — I never sit back without executing it. It doesn’t matter whether I get more followers or visits. Failure has become my sole friend. I learn from it every time I fail. Try not to repeat mistakes. Changing yourself is the demand you make when you start adopting better things in life.

A small task that helped me to understand the world how it is — It suggested that when you see things that you are doing, it helps to achieve what you think of an idea more than closed eyes. Try it out for yourself in Try this section. (Point 5)

Highlights:

Here are the highlights that I have made from my reading.

  • Brilliant students and brilliant innovators create their victories by practicing habits of thinking that inevitably carry them step-by-step to works of greatness.
  • The most fundamental ideas in any subject can be understood with ever-increasing depth.
  • By building on from foundations you will soon see your true abilities soar higher and faster.
  • We associate understanding with the element Earth because when we attain a rich understanding, we are standing upon rock-solid, from the ground. Earth is that which is under where we stand.
  • Mistakes are actions we definitely can take at any time. If you’re stuck, a mistake can be just the thing to unstick you.
  • Failure is a critical element of eﬀective learning, teaching, and creative problem-solving. Mistakes direct our attention in productive ways by forcing us to focus on the specific task of determining why the attempt at hand failed.
  • Mistakes and failure are not signs of weakness; instead, they are opportunities for future success.
  • The very act of creating questions, for yourself, is a profound step toward understanding — even if the questions are neither asked nor answered.
  • “Even when you do know the answer, asking, “What if…?” is a great way to see more and delve deeper.”
  • “What if…?” questions invite you to see the world diﬀerently because those questions force you to challenge the status quo and to explore the limits of your understanding.
  • The right questions can be incredibly powerful tools for understanding and learning. Great questions can lead to insights that will make a diﬀerence.
  • Questions give us a breath of inspiration and insight; thus, it is associated with the element Air.
  • New ideas today are built on the ideas of yesterday and illuminate the way to the brilliant ideas of tomorrow.
  • Solutions to little problems generate solutions to great problems.
  • Successful and eﬀective learners and innovators harness the power of the ﬂow of ideas, which suggests the element Water.
  • The ability to change is part of who you are, then you are liberated from worry about weaknesses or defects because you can adapt and improve whenever you like.

Tips:

The tips that can help understand the whole concept of the book:

  1. The building blocks of effective thinking,
  • Understand deeply: Don’t face complex issues head-on; first understand simple ideas deeply.
  • Make mistakes: Fail to succeed. Intentionally get it wrong to inevitably get it even more right.
  • Raise questions: Constantly create questions to clarify and extend your understanding.
  • Follow the flow of ideas: Look back to see where ideas came from and then look ahead to discover where those ideas may lead.

2. You only need to recall the classical elements that were once believed to be the essential parts of all nature and matter. Those elements, which predate Socrates and inﬂuenced Renaissance culture and thought, are Earth, Fire, Air, and Water. These elements are a reminder of the essential thinking that we need to learn. The 5 essential elements of effective thinking.

  • Earth — Understand deeply
  • Fire — Make mistakes
  • Air — Raise questions
  • Water — Follow the flow of ideas
  • The Quintessential Element — Change

Try this:

  1. Consider a skill you want to improve or a subject area that you wish to understand better. Spend five minutes writing down specific components of the skill or subject area that are basic to that theme. Your list will be a free-flowing stream of consciousness. Now pick one of the items on your list, and spend thirty minutes actively improving your mastery of it. See how working deeply on the basics makes it possible for you to hone your skill or deepen your knowledge at the higher levels you are trying to attain. Apply this exercise to other things you think you know or would like to know.
  2. The next time you face a daunting challenge, think to yourself, “For me to resolve this issue, I will have to fail nine times, but on the tenth attempt, I will be successful.
  3. Consider an idea or topic you are trying to better understand, and create a list of fundamental questions that will guide you to a complete explanation, including motivation, examples, overview, and details of that subject.
  4. With those questions (and their corresponding answers) in hand, prepare a minilecture and consider delivering it to some audience — family, friends, or even a teacher. Ask them questions to measure how well you understood and articulated your message.
  5. Grab a piece of paper and a pencil. Close your eyes tightly and write the sentence “I am writing as neatly as I can and any mistake I make is unintentional.” Now open your eyes and look at what you’ve written…it’s not perfect. Now repeat the exercise but this time with your eyes open. Your result will (hopefully) be much better. Writing with your eyes open is a diﬀerent (and easier) task than writing with your eyes closed.

Conclusion:

It does it all for ourselves. When I started to read this book, it took me 2 days to complete and hoped to change my habits. I kept discussing these concepts from the people I found and noted their ideas and questioned them. Along the way, I learned to control the flow of ideas and accept failures that I have faced in my life. Those series of failures helped me to raise questions about myself and my values. A person eliminates his/her values when they modulate their situations in life from survival to happiness. This doesn’t hold for all of them but most of us do the same.

Values are the ones that decide who we are and what we become. Acceptance is truely in the hands of us. When we follow these 5 remarkable habits in our life, we ought to see some major changes in life that can be adopted through minor decisions.

title: Few of the Biggest Questions About the Universe and Mankind
description: How we can answer some of the biggest questions of mankind — by Stephen Hawking.
imageAlt: A small telescope aims through a giant open orbit toward a few distant stars; humanity's biggest cosmic questions.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
If we look at what we did to the growth of humanity, we go as mysterious as it gets. The achievements that mankind has been doing for centuries are worth something and we always find a way to discover mysteries.

Mysteries are like particle physics, as long as we dig deep, confusing it becomes to understand more mysterious it gets to explore. I am fond of Astrophysics from the beginning of my childhood. Recently, I started to reinvent myself and in the process, I started to learn where I left off my passion in my childhood. I started to read books about physics and this article is about one of them, “Brief Answers to the Big Questions ” authored by Stephan Hawking. This is the last book of the great scientist. He gives us brief answers to think about the difficult questions we have in science. He made sure that we all understand science and experience the wonders of the universe.

Chapters:

  • What’s in it for me? Find answers to our world’s most ambitious questions.
  • Forces govern our universe — but a divine creator probably isn’t among them.
  • We can’t logically ask the question “What came before the Big Bang?”
  • There’s no easy answer to the question of alien life.
  • It might be possible to predict the future — but it’s unlikely.
  • Even light cannot escape a black hole — but something can.
  • To survive on Earth, we need to take immediate action.
  • We need to start colonizing space.
  • We need to be wary of runaway AI
  • Highlights from the book
  • Conclusion

1. What’s in it for me? Find answers to our world’s most ambitious questions.

We have made advanced developments in the history of mankind and we have a lot of infinite questions about the mysteries that are yet to solve. In search of those answers, we need to find ourselves as, where do we come from? Are we aliens to this planet? Can we colonize any other planets in the solar system?

In this book, he discussed all these aspects and his opinions toward it. We have many great scientists around the planet who solve the greatest mathematical problems every day but we all mustn’t be using our brain to its potential not at least together.

Let’s consider this article as the summary of the book along with my opinions over it.

2. Forces govern our universe — but a divine creator probably isn’t among them.

In this chapter, the author says that we as humans overrating and underestimating the capabilities of energy. We can explain almost all phenomena but still, some go unresolved.

We believe in religion and rely on science to prove all the theories. We think God as a conscious being instead of the ultimate power. In my thoughts, I agree with the author here. He is suggesting that the forces and the universal laws are governing the universe and we human beings are minute particles compared to what’s going on in the universe. Einstein referred to these laws as Gods. There is a religious belief about eclipses, lightning, and earthquakes before but now we have witnessed how they are happening.

There are still things that human eyes can’t see and understand but as long as we pray for the power instead of God as a person, religion cannot agree to work with science. They both need to work together toward the progress of unlocking mysteries.

We must understand how the universe began and how humans are created and what made us? Is there any knowledge that is already found and lost?

3. We can’t logically ask the question “What came before the Big Bang?”

Stephan Hawking explains that our universe is a huge entity and the origin of it remains as the mystery and excitement to know. Edwin Hubble’s discovery of the theory that Universe is expanding after observing the lights from galaxies across the night skies lead to the foundation of Big Bang theory. This supports that due to singularity the explosion happened.

As we know Black holes are the mysteries object where it wraps the space-time due to its high density where even time cannot pass through it. This concludes the understanding of Big bang and what was there before it. Still, the perfect answer is unknown but we can predict that nothing was there before it. Everything started after the big bang.

My theory is different from this question even though I agree with what Stephan Hawking is suggesting. But, I can call the big bang as the reincarnation of the universe. When objects move or expand at an accelerating rate, at some point the universe may contract and when it starts to contract, all the objects start to get closer to each other and wraps the space-time because of infinite density and gravity around it. It contracts and reaches the point of singularity like black holes. This leads to an explosion that causes the universe to restart again. At the point of singularity, time loses its value and all the forces come together and reach the same energy state.

4. There’s no easy answer to the question of alien life.

Alien life is a special part of the study that we humans are trying to master. We sent spacecraft to sail out of our solar system but still, the vastness of the universe is not ready to give up its mystery. After 7 Billion years of the big bang, our planet has formed and after 2.5 Billion years of our Earth’s formation, multicellular species were formed. About 60 million years ago humans are started to born. Before that about roughly 66 million years ago, dinosaurs got extinct by an interstellar event. The crater is now called Chicxulub — The impacted area that got dinosaurs to go extinct.

Still, out of our planet there are roughly 40 billion planets live in Goldilocks Zone — A zone that is helpful to form habitable planets — Not too hot not too cold from its star. There could be a possibility that life forms have existed before our solar system was born and got extinct. Maybe there are interstellar events that caused life forms to go extinct. There are chances that life forms are still developing.

We can ask these questions all day but we can never be sure of it not until we find the real answers. That is one of the problems in science. It never accepts belief. It only demands proofs and proofs.

5. It might be possible to predict the future — but it’s unlikely.

Particle physics or quantum mechanics that deals with the study of the movement of particles based on wave functions. Before 20th century, it is believed that based on speed and position of a subject, we can predict its future and later in the 20th century, it jas been disproved for particles that lead to an uncertainty principle — you cannot measure both the speed and position of a particle simultaneously; the more accurately you measure one, the less accurately you can measure the other.

This uncertainty made to define wave function that measures the position of a particle between 2 points. This is also supported by many discoveries and disproved the predictive future. In the next generation, we need to discover more about particles to understand how to locate exactly their position based on speed.

This doesn’t hold good when we come to the point of singularity — where space-time is warped by the density of black holes. There might be a technology where we can take help from or it is not yet invented. Either way, we need to explore and learn more together to uncover these mysteries.

6. Even light cannot escape a black hole — but something can.

We all know about black holes and how this is. We may don’t have the live pictures of it but using some wonderful technologies and observations, we were able to discover black holes. They are so dense that even light cannot escape from it. The author says, if nothing can escape it and black holes are the monsters, the universe would have swallowed by them because there are millions of black holes are present in the universe.

How is this possible? Why the universe is still intact even after 13.8 billion years. There is a possibility for the black hole which dies eventually at some point like every object has its end. Hence, we use quantum mechanics to answer this. Anti-Particles is the answer.

In 1974, Stephan Hawking proposed a theory about space filled with particles and antiparticles. These particles are responsible to bind the space just like threads in our clothes. With the interaction of them, black holes lose their mass and eventually disappear.

Either something more powerful than light exists in the universe or black hole has a death plan. Anyway, the whole universe is perfectly balanced and finely tuned to sustain.

7. To survive on Earth, we need to take immediate action

This is like a civil war and world war. There are categories of destruction. One is from the interstellar or interplanetary objects and second is from us inside due to fast-growing human negligence.

We are due from an impact from the celestial body based on calculations. We have the technology to detect if something is coming to hit us from space but we don’t the technology to prevent them.

With the huge difference that humans are making to our planet’s geological conditions, we need to start learning from our mistakes if we are planning to live on this planet in the future. Due to political and economic conditions, we are not able to save the earth to stop global warming. I read this beautiful article from Asmita Karanje, about “The politics of climate change is killing us”. She researched how global level extinction is near if humans don’t take action.

One more devastating cause will be nuclear weapons. If any terrorist group gets hold of all the weapons, the present nuclear weapons can destroy our earth several times over. What if all the countries make this treaty which states nobody manufactures nuclear weapons and the existing weapons must be disarmed and destroyed? At least we can make sure one of the many catastrophes are avoided.

8. We need to start colonizing space

As we are explorers and searching for many life forms. We expect to find another home for us and build it beside our planet. We can search for the place where the atmosphere is inhabitable. We have our limitations as well, which means we can only search for these places in our solar system until the technology is developed that can propel engines faster than light (FTL engines).

In our solar system itself, we have 3 known places that can be habitable by species. We are not sure yet but things are getting uncovered. Mars and Europa (Moon of Jupiter) and Titan (Moon of Saturn) are those places where we can sail and work to colonize our humanity in our solar system.

There is a barrier for all these that politicians think that they have more bigger problems to invest money in than for these projects. Colonizing space requires huge money and to operate it. My opinion is to crowdsource the funding for these kinds of projects. Out of 7 Billion people, each of them donates for this cause, we can get 7 Billion dollars to work on. This helps funding to get easy and we as humans can move forward.

We can collect 1 dollar from every human being every year. So, 7 Billion per year is a deal for space colonization.

9. We need to be wary of runaway AI

There are many movies and books are written about AI and there is a possibility that it can go rogue. Again this is in the hands of human beings. We are unique and far more intelligent than any other species. When we can come together, we can do wonderful things and invent breakthroughs. Now our mind is far more advanced than any other computer that human has build. But, in the last 50 years, the growth of computers and the internet is exponentially increasing. According to Moore’s law, it is improving at double speeds. If this improves for the next 100 years, AI can surpass the human brain with its computational abilities. When it grows to that level, we will be the inferior species.

Taking precautions while developing Artificial Intelligence is a must and we have to make sure it should always be a friend to human beings instead of a foe.

10. Highlights from the book:

  • Science and religion both offer answers to these fundamental questions, but come to radically different conclusions. One argues there is inherent meaning in human life, the other that our existence is little more than accidental.
  • Gods were seen as causes of lightning, storms, and eclipses. But now we have a more rational, consistent and verifiable explanation: our universe is a giant machine, governed by a set of unbreakable natural laws.
  • In nanoseconds, the universe went from an infinitely dense point, maybe smaller than a proton, to a rapidly expanding body that continues to grow today.
  • Einstein and his revolutionary discovery that space and time aren’t separate entities. Instead, they’re interwoven into a “fabric” we call space-time — the stage on which the universe exists.
  • The Most massive objects — like black holes — can warp space-time so violently that time itself stops.
  • By following the “chain of causality” back to its furthest point, we can prove the Big Bang couldn’t have a cause because time didn’t exist. There was no time for a cause to exist.
  • By the time Earth had formed, the universe was celebrating its seven billionth birthday.
  • Life took 2.5 billion years to go from single- to multi-celled organisms, which are needed for intelligent life.
  • What’s more, the theory of quantum mechanics seems to break down in extreme conditions where space-time becomes warped — like the interiors of black holes.
  • Black holes are formed when stars collapse. This happens because these giant balls of gas possess an incredible amount of mass — and the more mass there is, the more gravity accompanies it.
  • So if the universe has been around for billions of years, and nothing can escape a black hole, shouldn’t the cosmos be drowning in them?
  • In 1974, Stephen Hawking discovered that black holes release particles at a steady rate — and the answer again lies in quantum mechanics. His theory argues that space is filled with particles and antiparticles. They’re in a constant process of bonding, separating and then annihilating one another. The complex interaction of these pairs with black holes — particularly when partners are separated by the event horizon — causes black holes to lose mass, shrink and eventually disappear.
  • Global warming might be Earth’s most immediate threat, but we also face a greater one: nuclear annihilation.
  • Moore’s Law: It suggests that computers can double their speed and capacity every 18 months.
  • AI ethics has also become one of the fastest-growing fields of academic study. The most important thing to remember going forward, though, is that future safeguards must ensure machines will always be in the service of humans.

11. Conclusion

As final words, humanity is critical and it is in our hands to welcome it and to protect it. It is not about having anger with people together. Whenever you feel the distraction, let it go and start to explore the things that intrigue you. From the big bang to black holes and from humanity to the extinction of it. As humans, we have given the gift of curiosity and hunger to learn and explore. On the verge of knowing everything, we should not lose our path and values as well. We should be cautious while doing crazy things like grating AI the complete emotional consciousness. The human brain took almost 3 Billion years to develop from organic matters as we observe we are accelerating the development of computers that may cause “Hail Mary!” Someday.

To be human is to love and to be together. It is the law of attraction. We can do impossible inventions when we take a stand to be together. This is the biggest gift we can give to the power or God who created us — To serve the purpose of extraordinary species and to protect our home.

title: How Do We Define the Purpose of Life?
description: The purpose of our life can only be discovered when you start from nothing even after getting everything
imageAlt: A compass with a subtle heart-like centre and a single path through a generous open horizon; discovering purpose after starting again.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
It is quite common these days about how we work in our daily life. Obsession, Greed, Envy and Wishes to be rich or for the power. There are only two things that matter for many of us around here, i.e. Power and Money.

On top of Power, humans expect Money. It is commonly quite these days, If you have power, the money will come to you. As I witnessed, rich people stay rich and poor are climbing to the middle class and the people in the middle-class level stay the same. The real problem for the people is when the poor become middle class, the population in that category becomes more and when there is an imbalance between rich and poor, our life purpose loses its value.

As in democratic nations, only 1% of the people rule the rest of 99% of the population. This is quite common in developing countries. When people get hypocrites, the purpose of life deteriorates.

To regain the purpose of life and constantly reminding ourselves that we are here for a reason and we are here to make difference, we must be proactive, essentialist, technologist and certainties who looks at the higher things to count on. Who devotes himself to bigger causes and dedicates to the growth of humanity.

Let’s think, what is our purpose? Why are we here? What is our place? Is there any reason for our creation? Our purpose as humans become critical when we tend to work on ourselves with selfish instincts. In the pursuit of finding one’s purpose, most of us forget what we are there for and what we are supposed to do. We have given this beautiful planet and life to live on and help ourselves to strive together.

Eventually, with all the attraction we have, we forget to live instead, we just survive and persuade each other. Some people have values to help each other and some got a purpose to depend on others. There are 3 divisions in our life span with each having one purpose to complete.

Three Stages and Three Purposes:

Childhood, Adulthood and Old Age. Each level of the span has its purposes. In childhood, our purpose is to learn and plan for the future. Learning is a lifetime mission for all of us but learning in childhood makes us exceptional. It is a foundation for our growth and how we live our life. The reason every self-help books talk about changing routines, thinking, and habits is because of, less strong basement we made in our childhood. We play a lot and our environment never care about us and our future. Child’s cuteness and over care toward a child from the people around masks the child to explore the boundaries of humanity and the true purpose of life.

When the foundation is not strong, we must work hard to make things right when we grow up and reroute all our efforts that we need to make to find the purpose, of making our basement strong. What are we supposed to do in our adulthood? How can we find the purpose of life? Instead of living life to its fullest, we enjoy life by taking it for granted. We already know that we have given infinite attractions to enjoy our life and to live in it. Adulthood comprises of 2 stages as well. Youngster and Adult. At our young age, we tend to misuse our freedom and spend time in partying, hanging out and taking life for granted instead of being kind and continue learning. I know I sound like a nerd but that is true. I am not suggesting to abandon all the fun, I am just explaining how you can enjoy life with purpose instead of life without purpose.

Read books, gather knowledge, eat healthily, talk well, smile at people, be kind to them and never criticize. Along with all of them, now you have a chance to have some fun in life. Like partying, boozing and dancing your way out. Purpose of life is not all about fun, the very purpose of our existence is to make sure we thrive together instead of getting lost somewhere in the Amazon forest. When we focus less on purpose and concentrate more on temporal paradoxes, our life loses its meaning and backfires us. This affects the second stage of Adulthood i.e. Adults who are above 30years of age. As per the research, people who are above 30 are the ones losing more health or the ones who are symptom to lose health in their future. In our 20s we all take our lives for granted and spend much energy on doing unproductive work. After our body loses its immunity, it starts to deteriorate. Hence it is important to keep our body and mind healthy.

We loose childhood purpose from the environment we grew up, Adulthood gets contaminated by ourselves for not being better at laying the foundation at childhood and taking life for granted. We fall in love to enjoy the feeling and for the attraction that gives us temporary joy about life by neglecting the things that matter to us. Few are lucky to find love in their lives and most of us are not meant to be like that. I am talking about the people who don’t try to find their purpose in life. I have seen several individuals who are very smart. They choose to be right no matter how many people get hurt by their decessions. Those kinds of individuals are smart enough to experience everything in life from agony to pleasure at the right time. They get it to enjoy it and leave it. These people don’t stick to anything except for their purpose. I call this kind of people as pricks, betrayers, egoistic and selfish.

Finding the purpose of life is necessary but the way how we find it has its value as well. Finding purpose alone is less than good but helping others to find their purpose and along with them, when we find our purpose is the best way to accomplish our existence.

When we squander the opportunities that life gave us in these 2 stages of our life span, we tend to stay far from the third purpose i.e. Significance or Building legacy. If we brace ourselves and construct the city of dreams, the third stage will have its advantage of teaching others about the wonders you did in your life with experiences and nurture young minds. We all die someday with or without fulfilling our purpose. But, in the end, when we imagine our lives with the regret of not accomplishing our life’s true purpose, we tend to die with pain.

Don’t remember your life without you when you look back at it.

Create the life that is filled with purpose. First purpose is learning, second is making world a better place together and third is the significance or building your legacy.

Love the people around you more. Don’t run behind temporary love which has no meaning to it. Finding the purpose of life is significant and essential. You got to make the right choices at the right time when you are given choices to choose from. Remove the obstacle which creates 1000s of them in the future by identifying it right now. Be a good thinker. Take time from your normal life every day for 5 mins and think about your presence. Be mindful. The purpose will automatically find its way.

As we are at the end of this article, let’s understand one thing, the purpose of life is to do better everyday and lifelong we are dedicated to learning with unlimited possibilities to experience. Every breath we take is different and it has a purpose to live on.

Be the one who die with no regrets and the people around you talks about you and others who will be with you. Start your journey alone and end it with an army of family for those who you are the closest to their hearts.

Let’s join the hands of humanity to learn more and progress toward knowing a fantasy called life.

Keep learning and be stable. Stay hungry, stay foolish.

title: Physics and Cosmos
description: From Defining mankind to the end of cosmos where we all govern by scientific knowledge.
imageAlt: A fine spiral galaxy seen through two overlapping telescope lenses above a simple horizon; physics and the cosmos.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
For my science and learning obsession, I mentioned about Science and Religion in my previous topic. This time I want to write about Physics that related to our universe in fact how we are looking at, in our daily lives.

As far as history goes, mankind has started to look at the cosmos ever since the day of the beginning. I am not going to talk about the people who changed our understanding of the Universe as time passes. Listing out our achievements as one is the best way we can march with our humanity forward.

In the early ages of mankind, we all knew about the fact that earth is the center of the universe and all other celestial bodies revolve around it. This perception has the reason, Astrology. Our ancestors looked at the sky and the position of celestial bodies which includes stars, constellations, planets and other bodies in the night sky and was figuring out whether and time depends on the movements of them. They were also using stars to navigate and set up meetings with the other tribes on a yearly basis.

This raised to the fact that earth is the center of the universe where all the celestial bodies revolve around it.

This theory stood for ages and centuries. Even people thought the earth is flat. To disprove this theory, we experimented by sticking a stick on the ground in one place and placing another stick 1000 miles apart. At exact 12 PM, the shadow of those sticks is measured. One stick has no shadow because Sun was in the mid of the sky and on the other side, the shadow was inclined and found that shadow existed. This idea gave researchers to think, “if the earth is flat, at the same time, the shadow would have not seen from both the sticks from different places hence, the earth is spherical.” This experiment helped to create timezones later. Timezones are created depending on the incident of sunlight to the ground.

Now, let’s come back to the topic about the earth is the center of the universe. This is also disproved in the 16th century. It was explained as the sun is the center of the universe. It is called a heliocentric model. There is no evidence that how we got to this model but It is said that Nicholas Copernicus, influenced by Aristarchus of Samos from 4th Century BC. His astronomical ideas were often rejected in favor of the geocentric theories of Aristotle and Ptolemy.

There are a number of uncertainties in history. It is also believed that in Hinduism, their ancestors were predicted this model before any of the civilizations. It scales back to 6,000 to 7,000 years ago. In the end, truth matters and now we have the technology to prove those myths and verify them. Scientifically, from 16th-century modern astronomy was grown. When the first telescope was invented in 1608, things started to get an explaination. Looking at the sky using a telescope, planets and their moons are discovered. As far as the telescope can reach, we started to get proof.

With the help of explorers, we started to uncover the real shape of our planet i.e. geoid. Also, the heliocentric model got its upgrade as planets revolve around sun and sun revolve around our galaxy, Milky Way. All those planets revolve in an elliptical path. This has proved with the observations of weather changes on earth. When the earth is closer to the sun, the temperature on the ground increases and when it goes farther we encounter season like winter. We call perigee and apogee respectively.

Gravity and Space-Time:

That was a lot for the history of our discoveries. Now let’s come to the laws of gravitation. Which were proposed in the 18th century? Also, a reflection telescope has been invented. This is the commonly used telescope now to observe the night sky. It all started when Apple fell on the head of Issac Newton. He was 23 at that time and he took 20 years to prove that gravitation is a force responsible for the phenomena, not magnetism. Before this, it was believed that the attractive force is the only force that is magnetism.

Until he discovered this phenomenon, everyone believed that any object will be at rest if the force is not acting upon it. He disproved that all the objects move in a straight line unless an external force is acting upon it. This established the reason why planets revolve around the sun and moons around planets.

Even though it seemed that we are on the verge of knowing everything, there is a strange and interesting observation that has been made with respect to the speed of light. Newton’s laws of motion suggested that the movement of an object is relative to the observer or to the movement of something else. When it comes to light, the speed of it remains the same irrespective of the observer’s movement.

“It doesn’t matter who is viewing the light or how quickly they are traveling, its speed will always be the same.” — A Brief History of Time

This observation led to the theory of relativity and this includes time as one of the factors that affect the movement of an object.

The theory of relativity states that the laws of science are the same for all freely moving observers. This means that no matter what someone’s speed might be, they would observe the same speed of light.

What this means is that because the speed of light doesn’t change for observers moving at different speeds, observers traveling relative to one another would actually measure different times for the same event.

All these observations about the speed of light, celestial bodies exert gravity on every object that comes to its field, how they revolve around bigger bodies demanded more explanation. Hence, Einstein came up with an understanding of the gravitational force and given an explanation relating the three dimensions and adding time as the 4th dimension. This is called space-time.

An event is something that occurs at a particular position in space and time. So when calculating an event’s position along with the three-dimensional coordinates, scientists add a fourth coordinate to indicate time. This led to the modern understanding of space-time and how gravity works on another object.

Gravity is the result of massive objects curving space-time. A huge mass, like that of our sun, curves and actually alters space-time. Think of it like this: Imagine space-time to be a blanket stretched out and held in the air. If you place an object in the middle of the blanket, the blanket will curve and the object will sink a little. This is what massive objects due to space-time.

Creation of the Universe:

When this happened, great discoveries are made about the universe. We also discovered 3 other different forces along with gravitation. They are,

  • Electromagnetic force: The force exists between a magnet and a metal. We observe this every day in our lives.
  • Weak nuclear force: The force exists between electrons and nucleons in an atom.
  • Strong nuclear force: The force that exists to contain Protons, Neutrons, and Quarks at the center of an atom.

Concepts of these forces are simple, At very high energy called Grand Unification Energy, Strong nuclear force became weak and weak nuclear force and electromagnetic force got stronger. This lead to all these forces attains the same energy levels. When all 3 became equal, this led to the Big Bang. This formed our universe.

We study 2 subjects in our modern physics about the universe. One is Quantum Physics and the other is General Relativity. Quantum physics deals with the study of the nature of smaller particles like Atoms. Whereas General relativity concentrates on Gravity and Time.

These 2 subjects never cross the same roads, quantum theory suggests that all the empty space in the universe is made up of virtual pairs of particles and antiparticles. However, the existence of these virtual pairs causes difficulties for general relativity.

The Journey of Humankind:

Now we know how our universe is formed or at least we have an idea about what physics knows about our existence. As the final piece of information, I just want to take you all to the journey of Cosmos. Just broaden your mind imaging the place you are standing or sitting and look above. What do you observe? Don’t say roof or fan, I am talking about the open field. If you are not there, try to find one when you find free time. You already know that time is relative so let’s relate that to our Universe.

When you look at the sky, start to feel the field of view as you fly across the sky. When you reach the top of the atmosphere, you can view the whole city. As you go further, observe the earth from the sky. A blue body filled with white clouds. The view of our home from space is spectacular.

We do enjoy the view and the beauty of the planet when we go up there. In this infinitely larger universe, we find infinite mysteries. With the infinity, we add one more infinity as a constant to discover another infinity. This list goes on. As much as we explore, the value of infinity increases. Currently, we have to see up to 97 billion light-years in distances. Our universe is 13.8 Billion years old as we know but there are places where it takes more than that duration to reach but we can observe using a number of laws and workarounds like magnifying telescopes, sending telescopes to space to observe the cosmos.

The most popular space telescope is the Hubble Space Telescope. With the help of this, we discovered objects that are millions of light-years away. Now, humanity is on the verge of going further with the James Webb space telescope.

Along with Physics, the revolution of Optics is also an instrumental. As long as we discover infinities, we get close to another infinity.

Searching for Another Life:

After all these growths in space exploration, we can ask ourselves a question and we definitely deserve that, “Are we alone in the universe?”

Let’s discuss the probability, As we predicted there are 10¹¹ galaxies in the observable universe and in each one of them there are 10¹¹ stars and planets. So our planet is 10²² among the planets in the universe. Now, think about the question again.

I highly doubt that. We don’t have proof of extraterrestrials but we can definitely say the probability of their existence is more. Our nearest star is Alpha Centauri which is 4 light-years away from the sun and this is the closest star system to start searching for planets that can support life.

We are in the experiment of it but here are the statistics of it. We launched Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft to search for extraterrestrials in the 1970s. After almost 50 years, Voyager able to travel out of our solar system.

To reach Alpha Centauri, it stills needs 74,950 years this is because our technology engines are made to travel 0.00571% the speed of light i.e. 1/17500th speed of light. Precisely 17.142kms/second.

So, the probability of us finding alien lives except in our solar system is very less certain in this lifetime. There is a leap from us to reach our closest star within one lifetime that is 100years.

The project name called Project Longshot. It is under development in which the engine will be able to reach up to 4.5% the speed of light having a speed of 13,411km/s. With this speed, we can reach our next closest star Alpha Centauri B in 100years.

Conclusion:

We can say that reaching to other lives are difficult but not impossible. We may need FTL (Faster than Light) engines to travel across the universe. There are 7 Billion human lives on this planet and the people contributing to space exploration are just less than 1%.

Our humanity can achieve a greater feat when we can come together and more great minds are put to work. Let’s contribute and learn about the home we are in and let’s go and find some neighbors.

Stay educated and keep thinking about marching forward. To do impossible things we are creating Artificial Intelligence. The wit of the human brain and the speed of an AI can take humanity to the next level and someday we hope that we can see what is our place in this infinite universe.

If you’re alive, there’s a purpose for your life

— Rick Warren

We all have the purpose and we find ours when we learn about being great and driven by our values.

Happy reading and enjoy the infinite space when you feel you have less space.

title: How to Overcome Disappointment?
description: Non-fulfillment leads to losing faith in everything. So, expect less and live free.
imageAlt: A dropped paper boat is gently lifted back onto a calm stream, with a small repaired crease; recovering from disappointment.
imageCredit: Original illustration created for The Harithsa Notes.
html:
I write whenever I need something to cheer about. Having done several unforgivable mistakes in my past, still, I try to rediscover my potential and happiness in my journey. In our life, situations always go wrong and no matter how hard you try to convince yourself that things will be alright, you bow to disappointment in one way or the other. This has made its point in our lives. We work hard for something we love and we give ourselves completely to achieve our dreams, few people dedicate their whole life to something they can’t earn.

Contentment:

For example, if you work throughout your life in exploring the universe and beyond, as long as you keep uncovering mysteries; new twists and turn to take place in your understanding. New possibilities will be uncovered and your excitement becomes infinite. You started your journey in exploring the universe but you end up in doing nothing but just the laws that can help others to continue where you left off.

The point is if you look at the overall perspective, you ended up doing nothing. This is the disappointment of not accomplishing your goal. As you look into the things that you discovered in your journey you feel proud of laying a basement for your future generation to explore more. You helped exploration become easy by laws that you formed in your journey. This is the contentment in life. You started the journey having a goal that was impossible to achieve but in the end, you are happy for not getting to it as well.

Reason: In the journey, you discovered a lot of amusements that taught you the real meaning of exploration and on the way you have become the reason for others to start to explore more about it.

The universe is vast and it is impossible to explore beyond it in our lifetime of 100 years but we can take one step further in exploring it.

Disappointment comes when we lack in satisfaction. If you end your journey without laying the foundation for your future generation without exploring your goal, your life would be disappointed but now. My point in here is, most of us get disappointed in not reaching the goal of what we wished for but when we start to get satisfaction and appreciate ourselves in these things we do, we never get disappointed.

Contentment is the medicine for the disease called disappointment. In the above example, we discussed our life goals and how we do not feel sad even we don’t achieve our goal. The process is very important than the ultimate goal.

Smartness:

The same things incur for life as well. Life is vast we cannot achieve whatever we can. All 7 billion people on this planet want to be billionaires but very few of them work hard for it. Working hard is not the solution to achieve what you want, the smartness in putting efforts wherever you need takes you to greater heights. “Every hard worker is not a successful person but every smart worker is”.

We must know where to put efforts and where we shouldn’t to stand out among others. People say luck but it is not about luck in this world. Disappointed ones always complain about the ones who are smart and on their culture. Smart people are brilliant, they don’t show any disappointments in their lives coz, they always skid from them. They never stick to it.

Satisfaction or Contentment is the first step to get away from disappointment whereas, smartness is the second.

Love:

Life never gives damn about you when you are broke and disappointed. Even the person you love the most doesn’t help you in the time when you need that person the most. I am not saying that you need to trust and love yourself to get strength and confidence at the time of disappointment. We are humans and we love to go social and we expect people to be around us. Good people to be with us. We like to be in the middle of great people to feel ourselves to be lucky. Similarly, you deserve a person who you love the most to be with you when you need them.

There will be a situation where the person you love the most doesn’t love you. I have been in a position in my life. I was freaked out, alone, shattered, painful, utterly hopeless and strengthless to face anything in my life. There will be a time in everyone’s life like that. Not all of us get what we deserve, we may get less than we deserve and others may get more than what they deserve.

Love is the 3rd ingredient in life where it can get you out of disappointment when treated rightfully. When you start to love the person even after knowing that they don’t love you takes courage and if you are persistent in that, it eventually pays off and makes you proud of the fact and less disappointed about the fact.

Hope:

When life takes you down, we should have the strength to get back up. Listen to what your mind says. I wrote several articles about loving yourself and getting on with every obstacle in life. It is true that to love yourself, you need to be ready to accept failures and harms did by you from your mistakes. When you are sad or got disappointed by anything in life, we humans like to spend our time with the people we care about the most. When they are not available, we feel more disappointed by the fact more than the reason we had to be sad. We miss them and we get angry at them.

Hope is the best way to resolve your sadness when you are hit by life and its struggles. Keep telling yourself, “I can do this, this is not permanent and it will change”. This statement helps you to be in shape.
